Making something known by referring to a requisite so that the intention is understood is a request. Making a sign is an act of making a sign. ‘The third’ refers to lodging. ‘The remainder’ refers to requisites for the sick.

378. Pañcannaṃ [V 0.0341] sahadhammikānaṃ accaye dānaṃ na rūhatīti sambandho. Accaye dānanti “mamaccayena mayhaṃ santakaṃ upajjhāyassa hotū”tiādinā evaṃ attano apagame dānaṃ. Tanti accayena dinnaṃ cīvarādikaṃ saṅghasseva ca hoti, na bhikkhunoti adhippāyo. Gihīnaṃ panāti gihīnaṃ accaye dānaṃ pana. Idamettha dānaggahaṇalakkhaṇaṃ – “idaṃ tuyhaṃ dammī”tiādinā sammukhā vā “itthannāmassa demī”tiādinā parammukhāpi dinnaṃyeva hoti. “Tuyhaṃ gaṇhāhī”ti vutte “mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti vadati, sudinnaṃ suggahitañca. “Tava santakaṃ karohi, tava santakaṃ hotu, tava santakaṃ kārāpehī”ti vutte “mama santakaṃ karomi, mama santakaṃ hotu, mama santakaṃ karissāmī”ti vadati. Duddinnaṃ duggahitañca. Sace pana “tava santakaṃ karohī”ti vutte “sādhu, bhante, mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti gaṇhāti, suggahitanti.

378. The connection is: for the five co-religionists, a gift at the time of death is not valid. ‘A gift at the time of death’ means a gift at one's own passing, such as, ‘After my passing, may my belongings be for my preceptor.’ The meaning is that robes and so on given at death belong to the Saṅgha only, not to an individual bhikkhu. ‘But for laypeople’ means a gift at the time of death by laypeople. Here, this is the characteristic of giving and receiving a gift: when something is given face-to-face, saying, ‘I give this to you,’ or even in absence, saying, ‘I give this to so-and-so,’ it is considered given. If, when told, ‘Take this for yourself,’ one says, ‘I take it for myself,’ it is well-given and well-received. If, when told, ‘Make it your property, let it be your property, have it made your property,’ one says, ‘I am making it my property, let it be my property, I will make it my property,’ it is poorly-given and poorly-received. If, however, when told, ‘Make it your property,’ one takes it, saying, ‘Very well, venerable sir, I take it for myself,’ it is well-received.

379. Bhikkhu vā sāmaṇero vā upassaye bhikkhunīnaṃ vihāre kālaṃ kayirātha yadi kālaṅkareyya, tattha tasmiṃ ubhinnaṃ santake bhikkhusaṅgho eva dāyajjo sāmī hotīti [M 0.0408] seso. Sesepīti avasese bhikkhunisikkhamānasāmaṇerisantakepi. Ayaṃ nayoti yadi te bhikkhūnaṃ vihāre kālaṃ kareyyuṃ, tesaṃ santake bhikkhunisaṅgho eva dāyajjoti ayameva nayoti attho.

379. If a bhikkhu or a sāmaṇera should die in a nunnery, the dwelling of bhikkhunīs, the remainder is: in that case, regarding the belongings of both, the Saṅgha of bhikkhus alone is the heir and owner. ‘In the case of the remainder also’ means also in the case of the belongings of the remainder: bhikkhunīs, sikkhamānās, and sāmaṇerīs. ‘This is the method’ means: if they were to die in the dwelling of bhikkhus, the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs alone is the heir to their belongings—this is the method, this is the meaning.

380. “Imaṃ netvā asukassa dehī”ti dinnaṃ yāva parassa hatthaṃ na pāpuṇāti, tāva purimasseva, yo pahiṇati, tassevāti attho. Dammīti “itthannāmassa demī”ti dinnaṃ pana pacchimasseva, yassa pahiṇati, tasseva santakanti attho. Imaṃ vidhiṃ “vuttanayena ime sāmino hontī”ti etaṃ pakāraṃ ñatvā vissāsaggāhaṃ vā gaṇhe, matakacīvaraṃ vā adhiṭṭheti yojanā. Vissāsagāhanti sāmīsu jīvantesu vissāsena gāhaṃ gahetvā. Matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭheti tesu matesu aññe ce bhikkhū na santi, “mayhaṃ taṃ pāpuṇātī”ti matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭheyya. Aññesaṃ adatvā dūre ṭhapitamatakaparikkhārā pana tattha tattha saṅghasseva honti. Bhikkhumhi kālakate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare, apica gilānupaṭṭhākā bahūpakārā, saṅghena ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātabbaṃ. Yaṃ tattha lahubhaṇḍaṃ lahuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetabbaṃ. Yaṃ tattha garubhaṇḍaṃ garuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa avissajjiyaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ. Gilānupaṭṭhāko nāma gihī vā hotu pabbajito vā, antamaso mātugāmopi, sabbe bhāgaṃ labhanti. Bahū ce sabbe samaggā hutvā upaṭṭhahanti, sabbesaṃ samabhāgo dātabbo. Yo panettha visesena upaṭṭhahati, tassa viseso kātabbo.

380. When something is given with the instruction, 'Take this and give it to so-and-so,' until it reaches the other's hand, it belongs to the former, that is, to the one who sends it; this is the meaning. But what is given with the words, 'I give,' meaning, 'I give to such-and-such a person,' belongs to the latter, that is, it is the property of the one to whom it is sent; this is the meaning. Knowing this method—'in the stated way, these are the owners'—one should either take it on trust or determine it as a deceased's robe. 'Taking on trust' means taking possession with confidence while the owners are alive. 'To determine it as a deceased's robe' means that if, when they die, no other monks are present, one may determine the deceased's robe, thinking, 'It comes to me.' However, the requisites of the deceased that are placed at a distance without being given to others belong to the Sangha in each respective place. When a monk has passed away, the Sangha is the owner of the bowl and robes. Moreover, since the attendants of the sick have been of great service, the three robes and the bowl should be given by the Sangha to the attendants of the sick. Whatever light goods and minor requisites there are, they should be divided by the Sangha that is present. Whatever heavy goods and major requisites there are, they are not to be given away and are indivisible, belonging to the Sangha of the four directions, present and future. An attendant of the sick, be it a layperson or one who has gone forth, even a woman, all receive a share. If many attend in unity, an equal share should be given to all. Whoever among them attends with special care, a special portion should be made for him.

381. “Lohabhaṇḍe [V 0.0342] paharaṇiṃ ṭhapetvā sabbaṃ kappatī”tiādinā yojetabbaṃ. Paharaṇinti āvudhaṃ. Pādukā ca saṅkamanīyo pallaṅko cāti dvando. Mattikāmaye katakaṃ [M 0.0409] kumbhakārikañca ṭhapetvā sabbaṃ kappatīti yojanīyaṃ, dhaniyasseva sabbamattikāmayakuṭi kumbhakārikāti.

381. This should be construed with the text beginning, 'Among metal goods, excepting a weapon, everything is allowable.' 'Weapon' means an instrument for striking. 'Footwear, a plank for crossing, and a couch' is a dvandva compound. It should be construed that, 'Among earthenware, excepting a water-strainer and potter's work, everything is allowable,' for Dhaniya's entire earthen hut is potter's work.

Pakiṇṇakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of miscellaneous topics is concluded.

42. Desanāniddesavaṇṇanā

42. The Commentary on the Exposition of Teachings

382. Idāni desanānidassanabyāsena heṭṭhā avuttāni kānici sikkhāpadāni upadisituṃ “cāgo”tiādimāha. Bhikkhubhāvassa yo cāgo, sā pārājikadesanāti sambandho. Bhavati anenāti bhāvo, saddappavattinimittaṃ, bhikkhuno bhāvo bhikkhu-saddassa pavattinimittaṃ bhikkhukiccaṃ bhikkhubhāvo, tassa. Disī uccāraṇe, uccāraṇā pakāsanā desanā. “Channamativassati, vivaṭṭaṃ nātivassatī”ti (udā. 45) hi vuttaṃ. Idha pana bhikkhubhāvapariccāgoyeva pārājikāya pakāsanā nāma pārājikāya desanā. “Yo”ti vuttattā “so”ti vattuṃ yuttaṃ, tathāpi sabbādīhi vuttassa vā liṅgamādiyyate vakkhamānassa vāti vakkhamānadesanāpekkhāya “so”ti vuttaṃ. Yathā yena pakārena “chādeti jānamāpanna”ntiādinā vuttaṃ yathāvuttaṃ, tena. Vuttamanatikkammāti abyayībhāvavasena vā attho veditabbo. Idhāpi garukāpattiyā vuṭṭhānānatikkameneva pakāsanā desanā siyāti “vuṭṭhānaṃ garukāpattidesanā”ti vuccati.

382. Now, in order to teach certain training rules not mentioned previously, by way of exposition, illustration, and detailed analysis, he begins with 'relinquishment.' The connection is: that which is the relinquishment of the state of a monk, that is the exposition of a pārājika offense. 'State' (bhāvo) is that by which something comes to be (bhavati); it is the cause for the currency of a word. The state of a monk—the function of a monk—is the state of being a monk, the cause for the currency of the word 'monk'; 'of that' refers to this. The root 'dis' is in the sense of 'to utter'; an utterance, a declaration, is an exposition (desanā). For it is said: 'It rains on what is covered, it does not rain on what is uncovered' (Ud. 45). Here, however, the very abandonment of the state of a monk is the declaration of a pārājika, called the exposition of a pārājika. Because 'which' (yo) was said, it is proper to say 'that' (so); nevertheless, since the gender may be adopted from what was said by pronouns such as 'sabba' or from what is about to be said, 'that' (so) is said with reference to the exposition that is about to be stated. 'As stated' means in the way that it was stated in the passage beginning, 'knowing he has fallen into an offense, he conceals it.' The meaning of 'not transgressing what was said' should be understood as an indeclinable compound. Here too, the declaration, the exposition, would be precisely by not transgressing the rehabilitation from a grave offense; thus it is called 'the exposition of a grave offense through rehabilitation.'

383. Idāni vattabbaṃ sandhāya “eva”nti vuttaṃ. Ekassāti ekassa bhikkhuno.

383. Now, with reference to what is to be said, 'thus' is stated. 'Of one' means of one monk.

384. Tumhamūleti tumhākaṃ mūle samīpe. Paṭidesemīti pakāsemi. Saṃvareyyāsīti saṃyameyyāsi, saṃvare patiṭṭheyyāsīti attho.

384. 'In your presence' means at your root, near you. 'I declare' means I make known. 'You should restrain' means you should exercise self-control, you should be established in restraint; this is the meaning.

385. Nissajjitvānāti [M 0.0410] ekabahubhāvaṃ sannihitāsannihitabhāvaṃ ñatvā “idaṃ me, bhante, cīvara”ntiādinā [V 0.0343] nissajjitvā. Tenāti yassa cīvaraṃ nissaṭṭhaṃ, tena. “Imaṃ…pe… dammī”ti nissaṭṭhacīvaraṃ deyyanti sambandhitabbaṃ. “Imaṃ cīvaraṃ dasāhātikkanta”ntiādinā yojetabbaṃ.

385. 'Having relinquished' means: having known its state of being singular or plural, and its state of being present or not present, and having relinquished it by saying, 'Venerable sir, this is my robe,' and so forth. 'By him' means by the one whose robe was relinquished. The words 'This... I give' should be connected with 'the relinquished robe should be given.' It should be construed with the phrase beginning, 'This robe has been kept for more than ten days.'

386. (Ka) cīvaranti ticīvarādhiṭṭhānanayena adhiṭṭhitesu saṅghāṭiādīsu yaṃ kiñci cīvaraṃ. Vippavutthanti vippayuttena vutthaṃ.

386. (Ka) 'Robe' means any robe whatsoever among the double-cloak and so forth, which has been determined according to the method of determining the three robes. 'Away from' means having dwelt separated from it.

(Kha) akālacīvaranti anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimamāsaṃ ṭhapetvā sese ekādasamāse, atthate kathine tañca māsaṃ hemantike cattāro māse ca ṭhapetvā sese sattamāse uppannaṃ, kālepi saṅghassa vā “idaṃ akālacīvara”nti ekapuggalassa vā “idaṃ tuyhaṃ dammī”ti uddisitvā dinnaṃ. Itaraṃ pana kālacīvaraṃ. Māsātikkantanti akālacīvare uppanne ūnassa pāripūriyā saṅghagaṇādito satiyā paccāsāya māsamekaṃ parihāro labbhati, taṃ māsaṃ atikkantaṃ.

(Kha) 'Out-of-season robe' means a robe that has arisen: when the kathina has not been spread, in the remaining eleven months, excepting the last month of the rains retreat; when the kathina has been spread, in the remaining seven months, excepting that month and the four months of the winter season. It also refers to a robe given even in season, having been specified either to the Sangha with the words, 'This is an out-of-season robe,' or to a single individual with the words, 'This I give to you.' The other is an in-season robe. 'Exceeding a month' means: when an out-of-season robe has arisen, a grace period of one month is allowed for the completion of what is lacking, if there is a definite expectation of receiving one from the Sangha, a group, or another source; 'exceeding a month' means that month has been surpassed.

(Ga) purāṇacīvaranti yaṃ antamaso ussīsakaṃ katvā nipanno. Cīvaraṃ nāma channaṃ aññataraṃ vikappanūpagaṃ. Eseva nayo sabbesu vakkhamānacīvarappaṭisaṃyuttasikkhāpadesu.

(Ga) 'Worn-out robe' means one which he has used to lie down on, having made it at least into a headrest. A 'robe' means any one of the six kinds that is suitable for shared ownership. This same method applies in all the training rules connected with robes that are about to be mentioned.

(Gha) aññatra pārivattakāti antamaso harītakīkhaṇḍenapi pārivattakaṃ vinā.

(Gha) 'Except by exchange' means without an exchange, even for a piece of yellow myrobalan.

(Ṅa) gahapatikanti bhikkhūsu apabbajitakaṃ. Aññatra samayāti acchinnacīvaranaṭṭhacīvarasamayaṃ vinā, acchinnacīvarehi pana sākhāpalāsaṃ attanā bhañjitvāpi vākādīni gaṇhitvāpi nivāsetuṃ vaṭṭati, pageva viññatti. Cīvaraṃ viññāpitanti sambandho. Kanti āha “aññātaka”ntiādi.

(Ṅa) 'Householder' means one who has not gone forth from the household life, in contrast to the monks. 'Except on an occasion' means apart from the occasion of one's robe being stolen or one's robe being lost. For one whose robe has been stolen, it is allowable to wear even branches and leaves, having broken them off oneself, or having taken bark and so forth—how much more so is it allowable to make a request. The connection is 'having requested a robe.' As to whom, he says, 'an unrelated person,' and so forth.

(Ca) taduttarīti [M 0.0411] tato vuttappamāṇato uttari, acchinnacīvarena bhikkhunā kāyena vā vācāya vā abhiharitvā pavāritacīvarato tīsu naṭṭhesu dve sāditabbāni, dvīsu naṭṭhesu ekaṃ sāditabbaṃ. Pakatiyā santaruttarena carantena dvīsu naṭṭhesu dveyeva sāditabbāni, ekasmiṃ naṭṭhe ekaṃyeva sāditabbaṃ. Yassa ekaṃyeva hoti, tasmiṃ naṭṭhe dve sāditabbāni.

(Ca) 'Further than that' means further than the stated amount. By a monk whose robe has been stolen, from a robe that has been offered after he has made his need known by body or by speech, if three are lost, two may be accepted; if two are lost, one may be accepted. By one who normally goes about with an under-robe and an upper-robe, if two are lost, two may be accepted; if one is lost, only one may be accepted. For one who has only one, if that is lost, two may be accepted.

(Cha) appavāritoti [V 0.0344] gahapatinā vā gahapatāniyā vā. Vikappanti paṭhamaadhippetato mūlaṃ vaḍḍhāpento sundarakāmatāya “āyataṃ vā”tiādinā visiṭṭhakappaṃ adhikavidhānaṃ.

(Cha) 'Uninvited' means by a householder or a householder's wife. 'Causing a change of mind' means, out of a desire for something better, increasing the price beyond what was first intended, making a special arrangement, an additional provision, with words such as 'long or...'

(Ja) aññātake gahapatiketi bahūnaṃ vasena vuttamattameva purimato viseso.

(Ja) 'Unrelated householders': the only difference from the previous case is that this is stated in the plural.

(Jha) codanāyāti “attho me, āvuso, cīvarenā”ti codanāya. Ṭhānenāti kāyacodanamāha. Rājādīhi pesitena hi dūtena veyyāvaccakarassa hatthe cīvaracetāpanne nikkhitte tisso codanā anuññātā, codanāya diguṇaṃ ṭhānaṃ, tasmā sace codetiyeva, na tiṭṭhati, cha codanā labbhanti. Sace tiṭṭhatiyeva, na codeti, dvādasa ṭhānāni labbhanti. Sace ubhayaṃ karoti, ekāya codanāya dve ṭhānāni hāpetabbāni.

(Jha) 'By prompting' means by a verbal reminder, such as, 'Friend, I have need of a robe.' 'By standing' refers to a physical reminder. For when funds for a robe have been deposited in the hands of a steward by a messenger sent by a king or other such person, three verbal reminders are permitted. The allowance for standing is double that for a verbal reminder. Therefore, if one only gives verbal reminders and does not stand, six verbal reminders are allowed. If one only stands and does not give verbal reminders, twelve instances of standing are allowed. If one does both, for each verbal reminder, two instances of standing must be relinquished.

(Ṭa) suddhāni ca tāni kāḷakāni ca jātiyā rajanena vā.

(Ṭa) And those are pure black either by nature or by dyeing.

(Ṭha) tulanti catūhi tulāhi kāretukāmataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Atthato pana yattakehi eḷakalomehi kātukāmo hoti, tesu dve koṭṭhāsā kāḷakānaṃ, eko odātānaṃ, eko gocariyānaṃ gahetabbo. Tulā nāma palasataṃ. Gocariyā nāma kapilavaṇṇā. Idaṃ me santhataṃ kārāpitanti yojanā.

(Ṭha) 'By weight' is said with reference to the desire to have it made with four weights. In meaning, however, of whatever amount of goat's wool one wishes to make it with, two parts thereof should be black, one white, and one tawny. A `tulā` is one hundred `pala`s. `Gocariyā` means of a reddish-brown color. The construction is: 'Have this felt mat made for me.'

(Ṇa) tiyojanaparamanti [M 0.0412] gahitaṭṭhānato tīṇi yojanāni paramo assa atikkamanassāti bhāvanapuṃsakavasena attho veditabbo. Atikkāmitānīti antamaso suttakenapi bhaṇḍakatabhaṇḍaharaṇaṃ vinā antamaso vātābādhappaṭikāratthaṃ kaṇṇacchidde pakkhittāni atikkāmitāni.

(Ṇa) 'At most three `yojana`s' means that from the place it was received, three `yojana`s is the maximum for its transgression; the meaning is to be understood in the sense of an abstract neuter noun. 'Having been taken beyond' means having been taken beyond, even by a mere thread, without carrying goods, or even placed in a pierced ear for the purpose of counteracting a wind ailment.

387-9. Nissajjitvānāti vuttanayena vatthūni nissajjitvā. Athāti desitānantaraṃ. “Imaṃ jānāhī”ti gihiṃ vadeti yojanā. Soti ārāmikādiko gihī. “Iminā kiṃ āharāmī”ti vadeyyāti sambandho. Vadeyyāti yadi vadati. Imanti avatvāti “imaṃ āharā”ti avatvā bhikkhūnaṃ kappiyaṃ telādinti vadeti sambandho. Ādinti sandhivasena niggahitaṃ. Tena parivattetvāna so yaṃ kappiyaṃ āharatīti yojanā. Tenāti nissaggiyavatthunā[V 0.0345]. Dvepete ṭhapetvāti ete rūpiyappaṭiggāhakarūpiyasaṃvohārake dve ṭhapetvā sesehi paribhuñjituṃ labbhanti sambandho. Paribhuñjitunti taṃ bhuñjituṃ. Tatoti parivattitakappiyato. Aññenāti antamaso ārāmikenāpi. Tesanti vuttānaṃ dvinnaṃ.

387-9. 'Having relinquished' means having relinquished the items in the manner stated. 'Then' means immediately after it was taught. The construction is: he tells a layperson, 'Know this.' 'He' is a layperson, such as a monastery attendant. The connection is: he should say, 'What shall I bring with this?' 'Should say' means if he says. The connection is: 'Without saying "this"' means without saying 'bring this,' he says what is allowable for bhikkhus, such as oil, etc. 'Etc.' is included in the sense of abbreviation. The construction is: 'Having exchanged it for that, he brings whatever is allowable.' 'With that' means with the item to be relinquished. The connection is: 'Excluding these two' means excluding these two, namely, the acceptor of money and the one who transacts with money, it is allowable for the rest to use it. 'To use it' means to use it. 'From that' means from the exchanged allowable item. 'By another' means even by a monastery attendant. 'Of them' means of the two mentioned.

390. Antamaso tannibbattā rukkhacchāyāpīti sambandho. Tannibbattāti nissaṭṭhavatthunā kiṇitvā gahitaārāme rukkhacchāyā tannibbattā hotīti tato nibbattāti samāso. Ādito santhatattayanti ādimhi kosiyasuddhakāḷakadvebhāgasanthatattayaṃ.

390. The connection is: 'Even the shade of a tree produced from that.' 'Produced from that' means: in a monastery acquired by purchasing with the relinquished item, the shade of a tree is produced from that; thus, 'produced from it' is a compound. 'The triad of felt mats from the beginning' means the triad of felt mats at the beginning: the one mixed with silk, the one of pure black wool, and the one with two parts black wool.

391. Evaṃ ce no labhethāti evaṃ parivattetvā kappiyakārako no ce labheyya, so gihī “imaṃ chaḍḍehī”ti saṃsiyo vattabbo, evaṃ rūpiyachaḍḍako gihī no ce labheyya, sammato bhikkhu chaḍḍeyyāti sambandho. Sammatoti [M 0.0413] “yo chandāgatiṃ na gaccheyyā”tiādinā (pārā. 584) vuttapañcaṅgasamannāgato rūpiyachaḍḍakasammutiyā sammato bhikkhu.

391. 'If he should not get it thus' means: if, after having exchanged it, the one who makes things allowable should not get it, that layperson should be instructed, 'Discard this.' The connection is: if a layperson who discards money is not found, an appointed bhikkhu should discard it. 'Appointed' means a bhikkhu appointed by the formal act of appointment for discarding money, who is possessed of the five factors stated, beginning with 'who would not go astray through desire,' and so on.

392. Etānīti paṭiggahitarūpiyāni. Dutiyaṃ pattanti ūnapañcabandhane sati viññāpitapattaṃ saṅghe vattuṃ labbhareti padasambandho. Vattunti “ahaṃ bhante rūpiyaṃ paṭiggahesi”ntiādinā vattuṃ. Sesāni avasesanissaggiyavatthūni saṅghe ekasmiṃ gaṇe ca vattuṃ labbhareti yojanā. Bhāsantarenapi vattuṃ labbhanti na kevalaṃ pāḷibhāsāyameva, sīhaḷādibhāsāyapi nissajjituṃ labbhatīti attho.

392. 'These' means the accepted money. The connection of the words is: 'A second bowl' means when there are fewer than five bonds, it is allowable to declare the requested bowl in the Sangha. 'To declare' means to declare, beginning with, 'Venerable sirs, I have accepted money.' The construction is: the remaining relinquishable items are allowable to be declared in the Sangha or in a group. The meaning is: they are allowable to be declared even in another language; it is allowable to relinquish them not only in the Pāli language, but also in Sinhalese and other languages.

393. (Ka) nānappakāranti cīvarādīnaṃ kappiyabhaṇḍānaṃ vasena anekavidhaṃ. Kayo gahaṇaṃ, vikkayo dānaṃ. Kayo ca vikkayo ca kayavikkayaṃ.

393. (Ka) 'Of various kinds' means of many types on the basis of allowable goods such as robes, and so forth. 'Purchase' is acquisition; 'sale' is giving. Purchase and sale is `kayavikkayaṃ`.

(Ga) ūnapañcabandhanenāti ūnāni pañca bandhanāni yassa, tena, itthambhūtalakkhaṇe karaṇavacanaṃ. Yathākathañci pana pañcabandhano patto, pañcabandhanokāso vā, so apatto, aññaṃ viññāpetuṃ vaṭṭati.

(Ga) 'With less than five bonds' means by that which has fewer than five bonds; the instrumental case is in the sense of indicating a characteristic. However, a bowl that has five bonds, or the potential for five bonds, if it is somehow an unsuitable bowl, it is proper to request another.

394. Sammannitvānāti padabhājanīye vuttañattidutiyakammena sammannitvā. Saṅghassa pattantanti anta-saddena pattānaṃ ante bhavo lāmako pattoyeva gahito, nissaṭṭhapattassa vijjamānaguṇaṃ [V 0.0346] vatvā theraṃ, therassa pattaṃ dutiyattheraṃ gāhāpetvā eteneva upāyena yāvasaṅghanavakaṃ gāhāpetvā yo tattha sannipatitasaṅghassa pattesu pariyanto patto, taṃ pattanti. Tassāti katanissajjanassa bhikkhuno. Dāpayeti sammatena pattagāhāpakena dāpeyya.

394. 'Having formally appointed' means having formally appointed by means of a formal act consisting of a motion and a second announcement, as stated in the word-analysis. 'The Sangha's bowl' means: by the word `anta` (end), the inferior bowl that is at the end of the bowls is taken. Having stated the existing qualities of the relinquished bowl to the elder, and having caused the second elder to take the elder's bowl, and by this same method having caused them to be taken down to the most junior bhikkhu of the Sangha, whichever bowl is the last among the bowls of the Sangha assembled there, that is the bowl. 'To him' means to the bhikkhu who has made the relinquishment. 'Should have it given' means he should have it given by the formally appointed bowl-taker.

395. (Ka) bhesajjanti [M 0.0414] bhesajjakiccaṃ karotu vā, mā vā, evaṃ laddhavohāraṃ sappiādikaṃ sattāhakālikaṃ.

395. (Ka) 'Medicine' means ghee, etc., which has received such a designation and is allowable for seven days, whether or not it performs the function of medicine.

(Kha) gimhānassa pacchimamāse purimo addhamāso pariyesanakaraṇānaṃ khettaṃ, pacchimaddhamāso pariyesanakaraṇanivāsanānaṃ khettaṃ, vassikamāsā cattāropi adhiṭṭhānena saha catunnampi khettaṃ, imeyeva pañcamāsā kucchisamayo, itarasattamāsā piṭṭhisamayo. Piṭṭhisamaye pariyesantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ, kucchisamaye ca atirekaddhamāse katvā paridahato nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “atirekamāse sese”ti.

(Kha) In the last month of the hot season, the first half-month is the period for seeking and making robes; the latter half-month is the period for seeking, making, and wearing them. The four months of the rainy season, together with the determination, are the period for all four. These very five months are the 'belly season'; the remaining seven months are the 'back season.' For one who seeks during the 'back season', it is an offense of relinquishment with confession. And for one who, during the 'belly season', keeps it for more than half a month extra, it is an offense of relinquishment with confession. Therefore it was said, 'when an extra month remains.'

(Ga) sāmaṃ datvāti veyyāvaccādīni paccāsīsamāno sayameva datvā. Acchinnanti taṃ akarontaṃ disvā sakasaññāya acchinnaṃ. Bhikkhunopi cīvaraṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ parikkhāraṃ, anupasampannassa ca yaṃ kiñci parikkhāraṃ acchindato dukkaṭaṃ. Pariccajitvā dinnaṃ sakasaññaṃ vinā acchindanto bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo.

(Ga) 'Having given it himself' means having given it personally, hoping for services, etc., in return. 'Seizing' means, seeing that he is not performing that service, having seized it with the perception that it is one's own. For a bhikkhu who seizes any requisite other than a robe, and for an unordained person who seizes any requisite whatsoever, there is an offense of wrong-doing. One who seizes what was given up and given away, without the perception that it is one's own, should be made to pay its value.

(Ṅa) vikappanti “āyatañca karohi vitthatañcā”tiādikaṃ adhikavidhānaṃ.

(Ṅa) 'Modification' refers to an additional stipulation such as, 'Make it long and wide.'

(Ca) accekacīvaranti gamikagilānagabbhiniabhinavuppannasaddhānaṃ aññatarena pavāraṇamāsassa juṇhapakkhapañcamito paṭṭhāya “vassāvāsikaṃ dassāmī”ti dinnaṃ accāyikacīvaraṃ. Accekacīvarassa anatthate kathine ekādasadivasādhiko māso, atthate kathine ekādasadivasādhikā pañca māsā cīvarakālasamayo, taṃ atikkāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmita”nti. Kālo ca so samayo ca cīvarassa kālasamayo, taṃ.

(Ca) 'Urgent robe-cloth' means urgent robe-cloth given by one among travelers, the sick, pregnant women, or those with newly arisen faith, starting from the fifth day of the bright fortnight of the Pavāraṇā month, with the words, 'I will give a rains-residence gift.' For urgent robe-cloth, when the `kaṭhina` is not spread, the robe-season is one month and eleven days; when the `kaṭhina` is spread, the robe-season is five months and eleven days. For one who exceeds that, it is an offense of relinquishment with confession. Therefore it was said, 'having exceeded the robe-season.' It is the `kālasamaya` of the robe, being both a time (`kāla`) and a period (`samaya`).

(Cha) sappaṭibhaye āraññakasenāsane vassaṃ upagantvā viharantena bhikkhunā tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ [V 0.0347] aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ purimikāya [M 0.0415] upagantvā mahāpavāraṇāya pavāritatā, kattikamāsatā, pañcadhanusatikapacchi mappamāṇayuttasenāsanatā, sāsaṅkasappaṭibhayatāti evaṃ vuttacaturaṅgasampattiyāantaraghare nikkhipitvā sati paccaye chārattaparamaṃ tena cīvarena vippavasitabbaṃ. Tato ce uttari vippavaseyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “atirekachāratta”ntiādi.

(Cha) By a bhikkhu who, having entered the rains, is dwelling in a forest lodging that is dangerous—on the fulfillment of the four factors thus stated, namely: having been invited at the Great Pavāraṇā after observing the first; it being the month of Kattika; the lodging being of a certain measure; and it being suspected and dangerous—one of the three robes may be deposited in a house within the village. If there is a reason, he may be separated from that robe for at most six nights. If he should be separated for longer than that, it is an offense of relinquishment with confession. Therefore it was said, 'exceeding six nights,' and so on.

(Ja) jānanti jānanto.

(Ja) 'Knowing' means 'one who knows.'

396. Ādimhi viyāti paṭhamanissaggiye viya.

396. 'As in the beginning' means like in the first offense of relinquishment.

397. (Kha) antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya bhikkhuniyā hatthato khādanīyādippaṭiggahaṇe ca bhikkhūsu kulesu bhuñjantesu “idha pūvaṃ, sūpaṃ dethā”tiādinā nayena vosāsamānāya bhikkhuniyā anapasādanena ca sekhasammatesu kulesu pubbe animantitassa khādanīyādīnaṃ paṭiggahaṇe ca sappaṭibhaye āraññakasenāsane viharantassa pubbe appaṭisaṃviditakhādanīyādippaṭiggahaṇe ca pāṭidesanīyaṃ nāma āpattinikāyo vutto. Tena vuttaṃ “gārayha”ntiādi.

397. (Kha) When a monk receives edibles, etc., from the hand of a nun who has entered a house; or when monks are eating in families and a nun importunes them, saying, “Give cakes here, give soup,” and so on, and they do not dismiss her; or when one receives edibles, etc., from families designated for trainees, without having been invited beforehand; or when one dwelling in a dangerous wilderness abode receives edibles, etc., that were not previously announced—this is called the category of offenses requiring acknowledgment. Hence it is said, 'blameworthy,' and so on.

398. “Adesanāgāminiya”ntiādi “na desaye”ti ettha kammaṃ. Pārājikā saṅghādisesā ca adesanāgāminiyo nāma. Na āpatti anāpatti, taṃ. Katadesanaṃ desitaṃ. Nānāsaṃvāsanissīmaṭṭhitānaṃ na desayeti sambandho. Evaṃ catupañcahi na desaye, manasā na desaye, apakatattānaṃ na desaye, nānā “ekā”ti na desayeti. Manasāti kevalaṃ citteneva. Nānāti sambahulā āpattiyo “ekā”ti vatvā. Ekaṃ pana āpattiṃ “sambahulā”ti desetuṃ vaṭṭatīti.

398. “Not leading to confession,” etc., is the object of “he should not confess” here. Pārājika and Saṅghādisesa offenses are called “not leading to confession.” Also, that which is not an offense, a non-offense. “Confessed” means declared. The connection is that he should not confess to those of a different communion or to those standing outside the boundary. Thus, he should not confess with four or five monks, he should not confess mentally, he should not confess to those who have concealed their own offenses, and he should not confess many offenses as “one.” “Mentally” means merely with the mind. “Many” means saying “one” for several offenses. But it is allowable to confess one offense as “many.”

Desanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of confession is concluded.

43. Chandadānaniddesavaṇṇanā

43. Commentary on the Exposition of the Giving of Consent

399. Kammappatteti [M 0.0416][V 0.0348] uposathādino kammassa patte yutte anurūpe. Saṅghe samāgateti catuvaggādike saṅghe ekattha sannipatite. Ettha ca chandahārakenāpi saddhiṃ catuvaggādiko veditabbo.

399. ‘Kammappatte’ means suitable, appropriate, and fitting for the act, such as the Uposatha. ‘Saṅghe samāgate’ means the Sangha of four or more has gathered in one place. And here, the consent-bearer is also to be understood as included in the Sangha of four or more.

400. Chandadānādividhiṃ dassetuṃ “eka”ntiādimāha. Upāgammāti santiṃ āpattiṃ pakāsetvā tato pacchā upagantvā. Chandaṃ dadeti vakkhamānesu tīsu ekenapi bahi uposathaṃ katvā āgato chandaṃ dadeyya, kenaci karaṇīyena sannipātaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā kāyasāmaggiṃ adento pana pārisuddhiṃ dento chandaṃ dadeyya.

400. To show the procedure for giving consent and so forth, he says, ‘one,’ and so forth. ‘Upāgamma’ means having declared an existing offense, and then having approached. ‘He gives consent’—even if one of the three to be spoken of has performed the Uposatha outside and then returned, he may give consent; or if someone goes to the gathering place for some duty but does not establish bodily unity, yet gives his purity, he may give consent.

402. Ubhinnaṃ dāne kiṃpayojananti āha “pārisuddhī”tiādi. Pārisuddhippadānena saṅghassa attano cāpi uposathaṃ sampādetīti sambandho. Parisuddhi eva pārisuddhi, tassa padānaṃ, tena. Nanu ca pārisuddhitāpadānamattameva uposathakammaṃ nāmāti pārisuddhippadānaṃ attano uposathaṃ sampādetu, kathaṃ saṅghassāti? Vuccate – pārisuddhidānassa dhammakammatāsampādanena saṅghassāpi uposathaṃ sampādetīti.

402. What is the purpose of giving both? It is said, ‘For purity,’ and so forth. The connection is that by the giving of purity, one also completes the Uposatha for oneself and for the Sangha. Purity is indeed purity; the giving of that is by that. But is not the mere giving of purity itself called the Uposatha act? If the giving of purity completes one’s own Uposatha, how does it do so for the Sangha? It is said: By the giving of purity, by fulfilling the quality of a lawful act, one also completes the Sangha’s Uposatha.

Ettha pana catūsu ekassa chandapārisuddhiṃ āharitvā tayo pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, tīsu vā ekassa chandapārisuddhiṃ āharitvā dve pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, adhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ. Cattāro pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, tayo vā dve vā pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, adhammena samaggaṃ. Catūsu ekassa āharitvā tayo pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, tīsu vā ekassa āharitvā dve pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, dhammena vaggaṃ. Sace pana cattāro sannipatitvā pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, tayo pārisuddhiuposathaṃ, dve aññamaññaṃ [M 0.0417] pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, dhammena samaggaṃ. Pavāraṇakammesupi pañcasu ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā cattāro gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, catūsu tīsu vā ekassa āharitvā tayo dve vā saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, adhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇakammantiādi vuttanayameva. Sesakammaṃ vibādhatīti avasesasaṅghakiccaṃ vibādheti aladdhādhippāyattāti adhippāyo.

Here, when one brings the consent and purity from one of four bhikkhus and three perform the Uposatha of purity, or when one brings the consent and purity from one of three bhikkhus and two recite the Pātimokkha, it is an unlawful, divided Uposatha act. If four perform the Uposatha of purity, or three or two recite the Pātimokkha, it is an unlawful, united act. When one brings the consent and purity from one of four bhikkhus and three recite the Pātimokkha, or one brings the consent and purity from one of three bhikkhus and two perform the Uposatha of purity, it is a lawful, divided act. But if four gather and recite the Pātimokkha, three perform the Uposatha of purity, and two perform the Uposatha of purity among themselves, it is a lawful, united act. In the case of the Pavāraṇā act as well, when one brings the Pavāraṇā from one of five bhikkhus and four, having established a motion for the group, perform Pavāraṇā, or when one brings it from one of four or three bhikkhus and three or two, having established a motion for the Sangha, perform Pavāraṇā, it is an unlawful, divided Pavāraṇā act, as stated in the same way. ‘The remaining act is obstructed’ means it hinders the remaining Sangha business because the intention has not been obtained; this is the meaning.

403. Dvayanti [V 0.0349] uposathakaraṇañceva avasesakiccañca. Attano na sādhetīti sambandhanīyaṃ.

403. ‘Two’ means the performance of the Uposatha and the remaining duties. It is to be connected that one does not accomplish it for oneself.

404. Hareyyāti pubbe vuttaṃ suddhikachandaṃ vā imaṃ vā chandapārisuddhiṃ hareyya. Paramparā na hārayeti paramparā na āhareyya. Kasmāti āha “paramparāhaṭā”tiādi. Tenāti paṭhamato gahitachandapārisuddhikena. Paramparāhaṭāti yathā biḷālasaṅkhalikāya paṭhamaṃ valayaṃ dutiyaṃ pāpuṇāti, tatiyaṃ na pāpuṇāti, evaṃ dutiyassa āgacchati, tatiyassa na āgacchati. “Parimparāhaṭā chanda-pārisuddhi na gacchatī”ti vā pāṭho.

404. ‘He should bring’ means he should bring either the previously mentioned consent for purity or this consent and purity. ‘One should not have it conveyed in succession’ means a succession should not bring it. Why? It is said, ‘Because it is brought by succession,’ and so forth. ‘By that’ means by the one from whom consent and purity were first received. ‘Brought by succession’ is like how, in a cat’s chain, the first link reaches the second, but not the third. Similarly, it reaches the second person, but not the third. Alternatively, the reading may be: ‘Consent and purity brought by succession does not proceed.’

405. Sabbūpacāranti “ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā” tiādi sabbaṃ upacāraṃ.

405. ‘Sabbūpacāra’ means all proper conduct, such as ‘arranging the robe over one shoulder,’ and so forth.

406. So āgato ārocetvā saṅghaṃ pavāreyyāti yojanā. Athāti anantaratthe. Āgatoti pavāraṇaṃ gahetvā āgato bhikkhu. Ārocetvāti bhikkhusaṅghassa ārocetvā. Evanti vakkhamānakkamena.

406. The connection is: ‘He, having arrived, should inform the Sangha and invite them.’ ‘Atha’ is in the sense of immediate succession. ‘Having arrived’ means a bhikkhu who has arrived having received the Pavāraṇā. ‘Having informed’ means having informed the Sangha of bhikkhus. ‘Thus’ means according to the sequence to be stated.

407-8. Gahetvā hārakoti sambandho. Nāhaṭāti āhaṭāva na hotīti attho. Hārako saṅghaṃ patvā tathā heyya, āhaṭā hotīti yojanā. Tathā heyyāti vibbhantādiko bhaveyya.

407-8. The connection is: ‘the bearer, having taken.’ ‘Nāhaṭā’ means it is not brought at all. The interpretation is: if the bearer, having reached the Sangha, were in such a state, it would be considered brought. ‘In such a state’ means he might be confused or the like.

409. Saṅghaṃ [M 0.0418] patto pamatto vā sutto vā nārocayeyya anāpatti cāti sambandho. Ca-saddo chandapārisuddhiharaṇaṃ sampiṇḍetīti.

409. The connection is: ‘Having reached the Sangha, if one is heedless or asleep, one should not announce it, and there is no offense.’ The word ‘ca’ also includes the bringing of consent and purity.

Chandadānaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Giving of Consent is concluded.

44. Uposathaniddesavaṇṇanā

44. Commentary on the Exposition of the Uposatha

410. Duve uposathāti sulabhappavattivasena vuttaṃ. Tayo pana divasavaseneva uposathā cātuddasiko [V 0.0350] pannarasiko sāmaggikoti. Tattha hemantagimhavassānānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ utūnaṃ tatiyasattamapakkhesu dve dve katvā cha cātuddasikā, sesā pannarasikāti evaṃ ekasaṃvacchare catuvīsatiuposathā. Idaṃ tāva lokassa pakaticārittaṃ. “Āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabba”ntiādivacanato (mahāva. 178) pana tathārūpapaccaye sati aññasmimpi cātuddase uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

410. ‘Two Uposathas’ is stated on account of their common occurrence. But there are three Uposathas by way of days: the fourteenth-day, the fifteenth-day, and the harmony (sāmaggika) Uposatha. Among these, during the third and seventh fortnights of the three seasons—winter, summer, and the rains—there are two fourteenth-day Uposathas each, making six. The rest are fifteenth-day Uposathas. Thus, in one year, there are twenty-four Uposathas. This, for a start, is the natural custom of the world. However, according to the statement, ‘Newcomers should conform to the residents,’ and so forth (Mahāvagga 178), when there is such a condition, it is permissible to perform the Uposatha even on another fourteenth day.

411. Suttuddeso saṅghassevāti yojanā. Adhiṭṭhānañca taṃ uposatho cāti kammadhārayo. Sesānanti dvinnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vā. “Duve”tiādinā ca cātuddaso pannaraso sāmaggīti divasavasena, suttuddeso adhiṭṭhānaṃ pārisuddhīti karaṇappakārena, saṅghuposatho gaṇuposatho puggaluposathoti puggalavasena cāti nava uposathā dīpitā honti.

411. The connection is: the recitation of the Sutta is for the Sangha alone. ‘Determination and that Uposatha’ is a karmadhāraya compound. ‘Of the rest’ refers to two or three. By ‘two,’ and so forth, the fourteenth-day, the fifteenth-day, and the harmony (sāmaggī) Uposatha are shown by way of days; the recitation of the Sutta, determination, and purity by way of the manner of performance; and the Sangha Uposatha, the group Uposatha, and the individual Uposatha by way of individuals. Thus, nine Uposathas are elucidated.

412. Pubbakicceti –

412. As to the preliminary duties:

“Chandapārisuddhiutukkhānaṃ, bhikkhugaṇanā ca ovādo;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakiccanti vuccatī”ti. (mahāva. aṭṭha. 168) –

‘Consent and purity, announcement of the season, the counting of bhikkhus, and the exhortation; these are called the preliminary duties for the Uposatha.’ (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 168)

Evaṃ [M 0.0419] aṭṭhakathācariyehi vutte pubbakaraṇānantaraṃ kattabbe pubbakicce.

Thus, as stated by the commentary masters, regarding the preliminary duties to be performed after the preliminary actions.

Pubbakaraṇeti –

As to the preliminary actions:

“Sammajjanī padīpo ca, udakaṃ āsanena ca;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakaraṇanti vuccatī”ti. (mahāva. aṭṭha. 168) –

‘Sweeping, a lamp, water, and a seat; these are called the preliminary actions for the Uposatha.’ (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 168)

Evaṃ aṭṭhakathācariyeheva vutte sabbapaṭhamaṃ kattabbe pubbakaraṇe. Pattakalleti uposathādīnaṃ catunnaṃ aṅgānaṃ sambhavena patto kālo imassāti pattakālaṃ, pattakālameva pattakallaṃ. Kiṃ taṃ? Uposathādikammaṃ. Taṃ pana catūhi aṅgehi saṅgahitaṃ. Yathāhu aṭṭhakathācariyā –

Thus, as stated by the commentary masters, these are the preliminary actions to be performed first of all. ‘Pattakalla’ means that the time for it has arrived due to the presence of the four factors of the Uposatha and so forth; thus, it is ‘pattakāla,’ and ‘pattakāla’ itself is ‘pattakalla.’ What is that? The Uposatha and other acts. That, however, is comprised of four factors, as the commentary masters have said—

“Uposatho [V 0.0351] yāvatikā ca bhikkhū kammappattā,

Sabhāgāpattiyo ca na vijjanti;

Vajjanīyā ca puggalā tasmiṃ na honti,

Pattakallanti vuccatī”ti. (mahāva. aṭṭha. 168);

‘The Uposatha is fit when as many bhikkhus as are eligible for the act are present, and there are no shared offenses, and no individuals to be excluded are present—it is called ‘pattakalla.’’ (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 168)

Samāniteti sammā ānīte pavattiteti attho. Soti suttuddeso. Pañcadhāti nidānuddeso pārājikuddeso saṅghādisesuddeso aniyatuddeso vitthāruddesoti evaṃ pañcadhā.

‘Samānita’ means ‘properly brought about, established.’ ‘So’ refers to the recitation of the rules. ‘Fivefold’ means the introductory recitation, the Pārājika recitation, the Saṅghādisesa recitation, the Aniyata recitation, and the detailed recitation—thus, it is fivefold.

413. Vināntarāyanti rājantarāyo corantarāyo agyantarāyo udakantarāyo manussantarāyo amanussantarāyo vāḷantarāyo sarīsapantarāyo jīvitantarāyo brahmacariyantarāyoti (mahāva. 150) vuttesu dasasu yaṃ kiñci antarāyaṃ vinā. Saṅkhepenāti vinā vitthāraṃ. “Ettha dvīsu tīsu vā uddesesu visadesu therova issaro”ti vuttattā avattantepi vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Etthāti pañcasu uddesesu. Avattanteti therassa vitthārena avattamāne appaguṇe. Vaṭṭatīti [M 0.0420] saṃkhittena uddisitumpi vaṭṭati. Imināva yassa kassaci uddesakassa avattantepi vaṭṭatīti viññāyati. Dvīsu vattamānesu issaratte adhike vattabbameva natthīti dassanatthaṃ “tīsū”ti vuttaṃ. “Therova issaro”tiādinā idaṃ paridīpeti – dve akhaṇḍā suvisadā vācuggatā, therādheyyaṃ pātimokkhaṃ, sace pana ettakampi visadaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, byattassa bhikkhuno āyattaṃ hoti, tasmā sayaṃ uddisitabbaṃ, aññā vā ajjhesitabboti.

413. ‘Vinā antarāya’ means without any of the ten obstacles: the obstacle of kings, thieves, fire, water, humans, non-humans, wild beasts, creeping creatures, loss of life, or obstacle to the holy life (Mahāvagga 150). ‘Saṅkhepena’ means without elaboration. The connection is that because it is stated, ‘Here, in two or three recitations where there are differences, the elder alone is the authority,’ it is permissible even if not recited in detail. ‘Here’ refers to the five recitations. ‘Without reciting in detail’ refers to the elder not reciting in detail, lacking proficiency. ‘It is valid’ means it is valid to recite even concisely. By this, it is understood that it is valid even if any reciter does not recite in detail. ‘Three’ is mentioned to show that when authority is greater in two recitations, there is nothing more to be said. ‘The elder alone is the authority,’ and so forth, clarifies this: if two recitations are flawless and clearly spoken, the Pātimokkha is dependent on the elder. But if even this much cannot be clearly achieved, it depends on a competent bhikkhu; thus, one should recite it oneself or request another to do so.

414. Uddisante samā vā atha thokikā vā yadi āgaccheyyunti sambandhanīyaṃ. Uddisante āvāsikehi pātimokkhe uddissamāne. Samā vā thokikā vāti āvāsikehi samā vā thokikā vā āgantukā bhikkhū. Avasesakaṃ sotabbanti iminā ettāvatāpi uposatho katoyeva nāmāti dīpeti.

414. The connection is: ‘While reciting, whether an equal or a smaller number arrive.’ ‘While reciting’ means while the resident bhikkhus are reciting the Pātimokkha. ‘An equal or smaller number’ means incoming bhikkhus, whether equal to or fewer than the residents. By ‘the remainder should be heard,’ it is indicated that even with just this much, the Uposatha is considered done.

415. Uddiṭṭhamatteti uddiṭṭhaṃyeva uddiṭṭhamattaṃ. Matta-saddo avadhāraṇe. Sakalāya ekaccāya vā uṭṭhitāya samā vā thokikā vā yadi āgaccheyyunti yojanā. Sakalāyāti sabbāya parisāya. Esaṃ santike pārisuddhiṃ kareyyunti esaṃ āvāsikānaṃ samīpe te āgantukā bhikkhū [V 0.0352] pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kareyyunti attho. Atha bahukā ce, sabbavikappesu pubbakiccaṃ katvāti yojanīyaṃ. Vikappīyanti parikappīyantīti vikappā, avasesasavanapārisuddhiuposathavidhānā sabbe ca te vikappā ceti sabbavikappā. Tesu. Punuddiseti puna pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyya.

415. ‘Just recited’ (uddiṭṭhamatta) means simply what has been recited. The word ‘matta’ is for emphasis. The connection is: ‘whether the entire group or a portion of it has risen, or an equal or smaller number may arrive’. ‘The entire group’ means the entire assembly. ‘They should declare their purity in their presence’ means that those incoming monks should perform the Pārisuddhi-Uposatha in the presence of those resident monks. But if there are many, it should be connected as: ‘having performed the preliminary duties in all the variations’. ‘Variations’ (vikappā) are so called because they are determined (parikappīyanti); all the remaining procedures for the Uposatha of hearing and the Uposatha of purity are also variations, hence ‘all variations’ (sabbavikappā). Among these. ‘Recite again’ (punuddiseti) means he should recite the Pātimokkha again.

416. Itarānanti āgantukānaṃ. Itaroti cātuddaso. Ettha pana yesaṃ pannaraso, te atītaṃ uposathaṃ cātuddasikaṃ akaṃsūti veditabbā. Ayametthādhippāyo – tādise paccaye sati cātuddasikassa katattā tesaṃ yathāvuttatatiyasattamapakkhasaṅkhātacātuddasike [M 0.0421] sampatte terasīcātuddasīkattabbattā anuposathattā pana tattha uposatho na katoti cātuddasoyeva pannaraso jāto. Samānetareti samā ūnā itareti padacchedo. Itareti āgantukā. Purimānaṃ anuvattantūti āvāsikehi “ajjuposatho pannaraso”ti pubbakicce kayiramāne purimānaṃ āvāsikānaṃ anuvattantūti attho. Sacedhikāti yadi āgantukā bahukā honti. Purimāti āvāsikā. Tesaṃ anuvattantūti tesaṃ āgantukānaṃ “ajjuposatho cātuddaso”ti pubbakicce kayiramāne anuvattantu. Sesepīti āgantukānaṃ pannarasavārepi. Ayaṃ nayoti “āgantukānaṃ pannaraso itarānaṃ sacetaro”tiādiko ayameva nayo. Ettha pana yesaṃ pannaraso, te tiroraṭṭhato vā āgatā atītaṃ vā uposathaṃ cātuddasikaṃ akaṃsūti veditabbo.

416. ‘Others’ (itarānaṃ) refers to the visiting monks. ‘The other’ (itaro) means the fourteenth. Here, it should be understood that those for whom it is the fifteenth day had performed the Uposatha on the fourteenth day previously. The meaning here is this: because, in such circumstances, the fourteenth-day observance was performed, when the fourteenth day arrives (which is reckoned as the third or seventh fortnight as stated), and because the thirteenth or fourteenth day should be observed and is not an Uposatha day, the Uposatha was not performed there; hence, the fourteenth day itself became the fifteenth. ‘Equal or fewer others’ (samānetare) is a word division of ‘equal, fewer, others’ (samā ūnā itare). ‘Others’ (itare) refers to the visiting monks. ‘Following the former’ (purimānaṃ anuvattantu) means that when the resident monks perform the preliminary duties by saying, ‘Today is the fifteenth-day Uposatha,’ the visiting monks should follow the resident monks. ‘If more’ (sacedhikā) means if the visiting monks are numerous. ‘The former’ (purimā) refers to the resident monks. ‘They should follow them’ (tesaṃ anuvattantu) means that when the visiting monks perform the preliminary duties by saying, ‘Today is the fourteenth-day Uposatha,’ the resident monks should follow them. ‘Even in other cases’ (sesepī) means even for the visiting monks on the fifteenth day. ‘This is the method’ (ayaṃ nayo) refers to this very principle, such as ‘for visiting monks, the fifteenth day; for others, if different’. Here, it should be understood that those for whom it is the fifteenth day have either come from another region or had performed the Uposatha on the fourteenth day previously.

417. Atītuposathassa cātuddasiyaṃ katattā cātuddasiyaṃ pannarasuposatho katoti pannarasī āvāsikānaṃ pāṭipado jātoti āha “āvāsikānaṃ pāṭipado”ti. Itarānanti āgantukānaṃ. Uposathoti pannaraso uposatho. Samathokānanti attanā samānaṃ vā thokānaṃ vā āgantukānaṃ. Mūlaṭṭhāti āvāsikā. Kāmato dentūti attano icchāya dentu.

417. Because the past Uposatha was performed on the fourteenth day, and because the fifteenth-day Uposatha was performed on the fourteenth day, the fifteenth day became the resident monks’ pāṭipada; hence it is said, ‘the resident monks’ pāṭipada’. ‘The others’ (itarānaṃ) refers to the visiting monks. ‘Uposatha’ (uposatho) means the fifteenth-day Uposatha. ‘Equal or fewer’ (samathokānaṃ) means visiting monks equal to or fewer than themselves. ‘The root-standing ones’ (mūlaṭṭhā) refers to the resident monks. ‘Let them give as they wish’ (kāmato dentu) means let them give according to their own wish.

418. No ce dentīti yadi āvāsikā kāyasāmaggiṃ na denti, tesaṃ pana āvāsikānaṃ hiyyo uposathassa katattā ajja uposathakaraṇaṃ natthi. Bahūsu anicchāya kāyasāmaggiṃ dadeyyāti yojanā. Bahūsūti āgantukesu [M 0.0422] bahukesu. Bahi vā vajeti āvāsikabhikkhuparisā nissīmaṃ vā vajeyyāti attho.

418. ‘If they do not give’ (no ce denti) means if the resident monks do not grant bodily concord. Since those resident monks observed the Uposatha yesterday, there is no Uposatha observance for them today. The connection is: ‘They might grant bodily concord unwillingly to the many’. ‘To many’ (bahūsu) means to many visiting monks. ‘Or they may go outside’ (bahi vā vajeti) means the assembly of resident monks may go outside the boundary.

419. Sāveyya suttanti pātimokkhasaṅkhātaṃ suttaṃ vāyamitvā sāveyya.

419. ‘Recite the Sutta’ (sāveyya suttaṃ) means one should strive to recite the Sutta that is known as the Pātimokkha.

420. Sammajjituṃ [V 0.0353] …pe… udakāsanaṃ paññapetuñca mahātherena pesito kallo na kareyya tathāti sambandho. Kalloti agilāno. Tathāti dukkaṭaṃ atidisati. Āsanesu asati antamaso sākhābhaṅgampi kappiyaṃ kārāpetvā paññapetabbaṃ. Tele asati kapalle aggipi jāletabbo.

420. The connection is: ‘to sweep... and to set out water and a seat,’ if a capable monk dispatched by a senior monk should not act in that way. ‘Capable’ (kallo) means not ill. ‘In that way’ (tathā) indicates a dukkaṭa offense. If there are no seats available, even a broken branch should be made allowable and set out as a seat. If there is no oil, a fire should be lit even in a broken potsherd.

421-3. Paṭṭhapetvā dakāsananti paribhojanīyapānīyodakañca āsanañca sannihitaṃ katvā. Gaṇañattinti idāni vakkhamānaṃ gaṇena ṭhapetabbaṃ ñattiṃ. Teti aññe duve bhikkhū. Samattapubbārambhenāti samatto niṭṭhito pubbesu uttarāsaṅgaekaṃsakaraṇādīsu ārambho yassāti tipadabahubbīhi. Navena te evamīriyāti sambandho. Teti itare dve.

421-3. ‘Having prepared water and a seat’ (paṭṭhapetvā dakāsanaṃ) means having made readily available water for drinking and use, and a seat. ‘Gaṇañatti’ means the motion that is now to be established by the group. ‘They’ (te) refers to two other bhikkhus. ‘With initial preparations complete’ (samattapubbārambhena) is a three-word bahubbīhi compound meaning ‘one whose initial preparations, such as arranging the upper robe over one shoulder, are complete’. The connection is: ‘they should conduct themselves in this way with the new monk’ (navena te evaṃ īriyā). ‘They’ (te) refers to the other two.

424. Kattabbaṃ katvā pubbakiccādikaṃ sampādetvā navo evaṃ īriyoti yojanā.

424. The connection is: ‘Having done what should be done, having completed the preliminary duties and so on, the new monk should conduct himself in this way’.

427. Yatthāti yasmiṃ vihāre ekekassa pārisuddhiṃ haritvānāti sambandho. Ekekassāti ettha vicchāyaṃ dvittaṃ. Kiriyāya guṇena dabbena vā bhinne atthe byāpituṃ icchā vicchā. Ettha pana chandapārisuddhiharaṇasaṅkhātāya kiriyāya catūsu ca tīsu ca dvīsu ca bhinnamekekaṃ byāpituṃ sambandhituṃ icchāti vicchā. Itarītareti etthāpi karaṇakiriyāvasena veditabbaṃ. Tayo dve eko vā taṃ taṃ saṅghuposathaṃ gaṇuposathaṃ puggaluposathaṃ vāti vuttaṃ hoti. Ayametthādhippāyo – catūsu ekassa āharitvā tayo pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, tīsu vā ekassa āharitvā dve saṅghuposathaṃ karonti, adhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ. Atha pana ekassa āharitvā tayo saṅghuposathaṃ karonti, ekassa āharitvā dve pārisuddhiuposathaṃ [M 0.0423] karonti, adhammena vaggaṃ nāma hoti. Yadi pana cattāropi sannipatitvā pārisuddhiuposathaṃ karonti, tayo vā dve vā saṅghuposathaṃ karonti, adhammena samaggaṃ nāma hotīti. Tabbipariyāyena dhammena samaggaṃ veditabbaṃ.

427. ‘Where’ refers to the monastery; the connection is: ‘having brought the purity of each individual’. ‘Of each individual’ here implies reduplication for the sake of distribution. Distribution is the desire to apply a meaning separately through action, quality, or substance. Here, however, distribution is the desire to connect or apply the meaning of ‘one each’ separately to four, three, and two, through the action known as bringing the purity by consent. ‘One by one’ here should also be understood in terms of the action of doing. It is said that three, two, or one may perform the Saṅgha Uposatha, group Uposatha, or individual Uposatha, respectively. The meaning here is this: if, after bringing the purity of one from a group of four, the remaining three perform the purity Uposatha; or if, after bringing the purity of one from a group of three, the remaining two perform the Saṅgha Uposatha, this is an unlawful, factional Uposatha act. But if, after bringing the purity of one, three perform the Saṅgha Uposatha; or if, after bringing the purity of one, two perform the purity Uposatha, this is called an unlawful faction. However, if all four gather and perform the purity Uposatha, or if three or two perform the Saṅgha Uposatha, this is called an unlawful unity. The lawful unity should be understood in the opposite way.

428. Vagge samagge vā “vaggo”ti saññino vimatissa vā karoto dukkaṭanti sambandho. Vaggeti vaggasaṅghe. Vimatissāti “vaggo nu kho, samaggo”ti evaṃ vematikassa. Imināva kukkuccapakatavāropi upalakkhito. Karototi uposathaṃ karontassa. Bhedādhippāyena karototi [V 0.0354] yojanā. Ettha pana pāpassa balavatāya thullaccayaṃ vuttaṃ. Saññinoti saññāsīsena cittaṃ vuttaṃ, cittavatoti attho.

428. The connection is: in the case of a faction or a unity, for one who acts while perceiving it as a ‘faction’, or for one who acts while in doubt, there is a dukkaṭa offense. ‘In a faction’ refers to a factional Saṅgha. ‘Of one in doubt’ means one who is uncertain, thinking, ‘Is it a faction, or is it a unity?’ By this, one who is prone to scrupulousness is also indicated. ‘Of one who acts’ refers to one performing the Uposatha. The construction is: ‘one who acts with the intention of causing division’. Here, however, because of the strength of the evil deed, a grave offense is stated. ‘Of one who perceives’ means the mind is spoken of with perception as its head; the meaning is ‘one possessing such a mind’.

429-30. “Ukkhittassā”tiādinā vajjanīyapuggale dasseti. Ukkhittassāti kattuatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Nisinnasaddassa kammasādhanattā ukkhittādīhi kattūhi bhavitabbanti. “Sesāna”nti visesanassa bhikkhūnaṃ byabhicārena sātthakatā. Abhabbassa paṇḍakādiekādasavidhassa abhabbassa. Nisinnaparisāyañca pātimokkhaṃ na uddiseti sambandho. Sabhāgāpattiko tathā na uddiseti yojetabbaṃ. Vikālabhojanādivatthuto samāno bhāgo koṭṭhāso etissāti sabhāgā, sā āpatti assāti bahubbīhi.

429-30. By ‘of one who is expelled’ and so on, he indicates the persons to be avoided. ‘Of one who is expelled’ is the genitive case in the sense of the agent. Because the word ‘seated’ is formed in the sense of the object, it must be that the expelled ones, etc., are the agents. The specification ‘of the rest’ is made meaningful by its exclusion of the bhikkhus. ‘Of an incapable one’ refers to the eleven kinds of incapable persons, starting with the eunuch. The connection is: ‘and he does not recite the Pātimokkha in an assembly where such a person is seated’. ‘One who has a similar offense’ should be construed similarly as ‘does not recite’. ‘Sabhāgā’ means ‘it has a similar part or portion’ in terms of the basis, such as eating at the wrong time; ‘he has that offense’ is a bahubbīhi compound.

Chandena parivutthenāti ettha catubbidhaṃ pārivāsiyaṃ parisapārivāsiyaṃ rattipārivāsiyaṃ chandapārivāsiyaṃ ajjhāsayapārivāsiyanti. Tattha bhikkhū kenacideva karaṇīyena sannipatitā [M 0.0424] honti, atha meghuṭṭhānādinā kenacideva karaṇīyena anokāso, atha “aññattha gacchāmā”ti chandaṃ avissajjitvāva uṭṭhahanti, idaṃ parisapārivāsiyaṃ nāma kiñcāpi parisapārivāsiyaṃ, chandassa pana avissaṭṭhattā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

Regarding ‘enveloped by consent’: here, there are four kinds of interruption: interruption of the assembly, interruption by night, interruption of consent, and interruption of disposition. In this case, monks have gathered for some business, but due to some urgent matter like a storm arising, there is no opportunity. Then, without having released their consent, they rise, saying, ‘Let us go elsewhere.’ This is called interruption of the assembly. Although it is an interruption of the assembly, because the consent has not been released, it is still permissible to perform the formal act.

“Yāva pana sabbe sannipatanti, tāva dhammaṃ suṇissāmā”ti ekaṃ ajjhesanti, tasmiṃ dhammakathaṃ kathenteyeva aruṇo uggacchati, sace cātuddasikaṃ kātuṃ nisinnā, pannarasoti kātuṃ vaṭṭati, sace pannarasikaṃ kātuṃ nisinnā, pāṭipade anuposathe uposathaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, aññaṃ pana saṅghakiccaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, idaṃ rattipārivāsiyaṃ nāma.

They request a certain monk, saying, ‘Until everyone gathers, let us listen to the Dhamma.’ While he is giving the Dhamma talk, dawn breaks. If they sat down to perform the fourteenth-day observance, it is permissible to perform the fifteenth-day observance. If they sat down to perform the fifteenth-day observance, it is not permissible to perform the Uposatha on the following day, which is a non-Uposatha day. However, it is permissible to perform other Saṅgha business. This is called interruption by night.

Evaṃ pana nisinne koci nakkhattapāṭhako bhikkhu “ajja nakkhattaṃ dāruṇaṃ, imaṃ kammaṃ mā karothā”ti vadati, te tassa vacanena chandaṃ vissajjetvā tattheva nisinnā honti, athañño āgantvā “nakkhattaṃ paṭimānentaṃ, attho bālaṃ upaccagā”ti (jā. 1.1.49) vatvā “kiṃ nakkhattena, karothā”ti vadati, idaṃ chandapārivāsiyañceva ajjhāsayapārivāsiyañca. Ekasmiṃ pārivāsiye puna chandapārisuddhiṃ ānetvā kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

But while they are sitting thus, a certain monk who is an astrologer says, ‘Today the constellation is fierce; do not perform this act.’ They, by his word, release their consent and remain seated right there. Then another monk arrives and, having said, ‘While waiting for the constellation, the goal has passed the fool by’ (Jā. 1.1.49), says, ‘What of the constellation? Do it!’ This is both interruption of consent and interruption of disposition. In the case of such an interruption, it is permissible to perform the act by bringing the purity of consent again.

431. Āpannañca [V 0.0355] vematikañca adesayitvā vā nāvikatvā vā uposathaṃ kātuṃ na ca kappatīti sambandho. Nāvikatvāti garukāpattiṃ anāvikatvā. Na cāti neva.

431. The connection is: it is not permissible to perform the Uposatha without having declared a committed offense or one about which there is doubt, or without having confessed it. ‘Not having confessed’ means not having confessed a grave offense. ‘And not’ means ‘not at all’.

432. Aṭṭhitoposathāti aṭṭhito avissaṭṭho uposatho yasminti bahubbīhi. Tadahūti tasmiṃ uposathadivase. Antarāyaṃ vā saṅghaṃ vā vinā adhiṭṭhātuṃ sīmameva vā [M 0.0425] na vajeti yojanā. Adhiṭṭhātunti iminā gaṇuposathampi upalakkheti. Sīmanti iminā nadimpi.

432. ‘Aṭṭhitoposatha’ is a bahubbīhi compound meaning ‘that in which the Uposatha is established, not relinquished’. ‘On that day’ means on that Uposatha day. The construction is: ‘without an obstacle or the Saṅgha, one does not go even to the boundary to determine the Uposatha’. By ‘to determine’, the group Uposatha is also indicated. By ‘boundary’, a river is also indicated.

Uposathaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Uposatha is concluded.

45. Pavāraṇāniddesavaṇṇanā

45. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Pavāraṇā

433. “Aññamaññappavāraṇā”tyādīnaṃ aññamaññehi kātabbā pavāraṇā. Tattha tiṇṇaṃ catunnañca gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā aññamaññappavāraṇā, dvinnaṃ pana aṭṭhapetvāva. Adhiṭṭhānanti adhiṭṭhānappavāraṇā, yupaccayantānaṃ bhāve niyatanapuṃsakattā “adhiṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Sesā pañcādīhi kātabbā avasesā saṅghappavāraṇā saṅghavasena ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā kātabbā. Etena navasu saṅghappavāraṇādayo tisso dassitā. Nava hi pavāraṇā cātuddasī pannarasī sāmaggīti divasavasena, tevācī dvevācī ekavācīti kattabbākāravasena, saṅghe pavāraṇā, gaṇe pavāraṇā, puggale pavāraṇāti kārakavasena ca. Tattha purimavassaṃvutthānaṃ pubbakattikapuṇṇamā vā tesaṃyeva sace bhaṇḍanakārakehi upaddutā pavāraṇaṃ paccukkaḍḍhanti, atha kattikamāsassa kāḷapakkhacātuddaso vā pacchimakattikapuṇṇamā vā pacchimavassaṃvutthānañca pacchimakattikapuṇṇamā eva vā pavāraṇādivasā honti. Idaṃ pana pakaticārittaṃ. Tathārūpappaccaye sati dvinnaṃ kattikapuṇṇamānaṃ purimesu cātuddasesupi pavāraṇaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Bhinnassa pana saṅghassa sāmaggiyaṃ yo koci divaso pavāraṇādivaso hoti. Imā divasavasena tisso pavāraṇā. Kattabbākāravasena pana vakkhamānanayena viññātabbā.

433. ‘Mutual invitation’ and so on means the invitation that should be made among one another. Therein, for groups of three and four, it is a mutual invitation, having established a motion for the group; but for a group of two, it is done without establishing one. ‘Determination’ refers to the invitation by determination. Because words ending in the suffix ‘-yu’ are of fixed neuter gender when in the sense of ‘state’, it is called ‘determination’. The remaining Saṅgha-Pavāraṇā, to be done by the remaining five or more, should be done by establishing a motion in accordance with the Saṅgha. By this, three of the nine kinds of Pavāraṇā—the Saṅgha-Pavāraṇā and so on—are indicated. For there are nine Pavāraṇās: the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the day of unity, based on the day; the threefold, twofold, and single utterance, based on the manner of performance; and the Saṅgha-Pavāraṇā, group Pavāraṇā, and individual Pavāraṇā, based on the agent. Here, for those who have completed the earlier rains-retreat, the Pubbakattika full moon is the time; but if they, being harassed by quarrel-makers, postpone the Pavāraṇā, then either the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kattika or the later Kattika full moon is the time. And for those who have completed the later rains-retreat, the later Kattika full moon itself is the day of Pavāraṇā. This, however, is the normal custom. When such a condition is present, it is permissible to perform the Pavāraṇā also on the fourteenth days that precede the two Kattika full moons. But for a divided Saṅgha, whatever day they achieve unity becomes the Pavāraṇā day. These are the three Pavāraṇās based on the day. As for those based on the manner of performance, they should be understood according to the explanation to be given.

434. “Pubbakicce”tiādīsu –

434. In such as ‘preliminary duties’:

“Sammajjanī [V 0.0356] padīpo ca, udakaṃ āsanena ca;

Pavāraṇāya etāni, pubbakaraṇanti vuccati.

“Sweeping, a lamp, water, and a seat; these for the Pavāraṇā are called the preliminary preparations.”

“Chandappavāraṇā [M 0.0426] utukkhānaṃ, bhikkhugaṇanā ca ovādo;

Pavāraṇāya etāni, pubbakiccanti vuccati.

“Bringing consent and Pavāraṇā, the declaration of the season, the counting of monks, and the exhortation; these for the Pavāraṇā are called the preliminary duties.”

“Pavāraṇā yāvatikā ca bhikkhū kammappattā,

Sabhāgāpattiyo ca na vijjanti;

Vajjanīyā ca puggalā tasmiṃ na honti,

Pattakallanti vuccatī”ti. –

“The Pavāraṇā, when as many bhikkhus as are fit for the act are present, and similar offenses do not exist, and persons to be avoided are not in that assembly, is called ‘timely and fit’.”

Evaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttā pubbakiccādayo veditabbā. Ñattinti idāni vakkhamānaṃ sāmaññaṃ saṅghañattiṃ. Evaṃ pana ñattiyā ṭhapitāya kāraṇe sati tevācikadvevācikaekavācikasamānavassikavasenapi pavāretuṃ vaṭṭati. Ayameva pana ñatti “saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti ettha “saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāreyya, saṅgho dvevācikaṃ pavāreyya, saṅgho ekavācikaṃ pavāreyya, saṅgho samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”tipi ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati. Cātuddasiyaṃ pana sāmaggiyañca “cātuddasī sāmaggī”ti vattabbaṃ.

Thus, the preliminary duties and so on, as stated in the commentary, should be understood. 'Motion' refers to the general Saṅgha-motion that will now be explained. Once such a motion is established, when there is a reason, it is permissible to hold Pavāraṇā by way of three utterances, two utterances, one utterance, or for those of the same rains-residence. Furthermore, this same motion, 'Let the Saṅgha hold Pavāraṇā,' can also be established thus: 'Let the Saṅgha hold Pavāraṇā with three utterances, let the Saṅgha hold Pavāraṇā with two utterances, let the Saṅgha hold Pavāraṇā with one utterance, let the Saṅgha hold Pavāraṇā for those of the same rains-residence.' On the fourteenth, when there is concord, it should be stated, 'The fourteenth is with concord.'

437. Theresu ukkuṭikaṃ nisajja pavārentesu navo yāva sayaṃ pavāreti, tāva ukkuṭiko eva acchatūti yojanā. Acchatūti nisīdeyya.

437. When the elders are inviting while sitting on their heels, the new monk should remain sitting on his heels until he himself invites—this is the construction. 'Should remain' means he should sit.

440-2. Dhammasākacchā ca kalaho cāti dvando. Rattiyā khepitabhāvato tevācikāya okāse asati dasavidhe vā antarāye sati “suṇātu me…pe… samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti anurūpato ñattiṃ vatvā yathāṭhapitañattiyā anurūpena pavāreyyāti sambandho veditabbo. Anurūpatoti “suṇātu me…pe… dānaṃ dentehi ratti khepitā, sace…pe… ratti vibhāyissati, yadi saṅghassa pattakalla”ntiādinā tena khepitarattiyā anurūpena. “Suṇātu me bhante saṅgho, ayaṃ rājantarāyo, sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ…pe… saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ [M 0.0427] rājantarāyo bhavissati, yadi saṅghassa pattakalla”ntiādinā rājantarāyādīnaṃ [V 0.0357] anurūpena vāti attho. “Athāyaṃ brahmacariyantarāyo bhavissatī”ti pana peyyālavasena ante vuttaṃ brahmacariyantarāyaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ. “Dvevācika”ntiādikaṃ pana visuṃ visuṃ vattabbampi laṅghanakkamena sampiṇḍetvā vuttaṃ. Vacanasamaye pana “dvevācikaṃ pavāreyya”iccādinā vattabbaṃ. Āgaccheyyuṃ yadi samāādikā cāti “āgaccheyyuṃ yadi samā”iccādayo uposathe vuttā gāthāyo ca. Etthāti etissaṃ pavāraṇāyaṃ. Ayameva ca āharaṇakkamo –

440-2. 'Discussion of Dhamma and quarrel'—this is a dvandva compound. Since the night was spent, if there is no opportunity for the three utterances, or if there is one of the ten obstacles, then, having spoken the appropriate motion, 'May the Saṅgha listen to me... may the Saṅgha invite for those of the same rains-residence,' one should invite according to the established motion—this connection should be understood. 'Appropriate' means according to the night spent, as in, 'May the Saṅgha listen to me... while giving gifts, the night was spent. If... the night will pass, if it is agreeable to the Saṅgha,' and so on. Or, 'May the Saṅgha listen to me, venerable sirs. There is this royal danger. If the Saṅgha were to invite by three utterances... this royal danger would occur. If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha,' and so on—this is the meaning regarding royal dangers and so on. 'Then this danger to the holy life will occur'—this is said by way of the ellipsis marker, taking the danger to the holy life mentioned at the end. 'Two utterances,' etc., though each should be spoken separately, are stated concisely by way of abbreviation. At the time of speaking, one should say, 'May the Saṅgha invite with two utterances,' and so on. 'Should they arrive, being a complete group'—these verses about 'should they arrive, being a complete group,' etc., were spoken regarding the Uposatha. Here—in this Pavāraṇā. This is the order of recitation.

Āgaccheyyuṃ yadi samā, pavārenteva thokikā;

Pavāritā te suppavāritā, aññehi ca pavāriyaṃ;

Pavāritesu sakalā-yekaccāyuṭṭhitāya vā.

Should they arrive, being a complete group, let them invite, even if few; Those who have invited have invited well, and it should be invited by others; When all have invited, or when some have arisen...

Pavāreyyuñca te tesaṃ, santike bahukā sace;

Katvā sabbavikappesu, pubbakiccaṃ punuddiseti.

And they should invite in the presence of those others, if they are many. Having made all the arrangements, the preliminary duties are then announced again.

“Āvāsikānaṃ pannaraso”tiādikā gāthāyo pana etthāpi samānā.

The verses beginning with 'For the residents, the fifteenth,' etc., are the same here also.

443. Ñattiṃ vatvāti vakkhamānagaṇañattiṃ vatvā.

443. 'Having stated the motion'—having stated the group-motion that will be explained.

444. Samudīriyāti aññe dve tayo vā vakkhamānakkamena vattabbā.

444. 'Should be uttered'—two or three others should be spoken in the order about to be explained.

446-8. Kattabbaṃ katvāti yojetabbaṃ. Kattabbanti pubbakiccādikaṃ. Navenapi “ahaṃ bhante…pe… paṭikarissāmī”ti thero īriyoti yojetabbaṃ. Evanti idāni vakkhamānaṃ parāmasati.

446-8. 'Having done what should be done' should be construed. 'What should be done' refers to preliminary duties and the like. It should be construed that the new monk also says to the elder, 'Venerable sir... I will make amends.' 'Thus' refers to what is about to be said.

449. “Yasmi”ntiādi vuttanayattā uttānameva.

449. 'In which,' etc.—the meaning is clear, as the method has already been stated.

450. Gāthāyoti [M 0.0428] “vagge samagge vaggoti, saññino”tiādikā heṭṭhā vuttagāthāyo vā. Ayaṃ panettha viseso – karototi ettha pavāraṇaṃ karototi attho gahetabbo. Tatiya gāthāya [V 0.0358] “pātimokkhaṃ na uddise”ti apanetvā “no kareyya pavāraṇa”nti padaṃ pakkhipitabbaṃ. Catutthagāthāya “anuposathe”tiādigāthābandhaṃ apanetvā “neva pavāraṇe kātuṃ, sā kappati pavāraṇā”ti pakkhipitabbaṃ. Pañcamagāthāya “aṭṭhitoposathāvāsā”ti apanetvā “pavāraṇāṭhitāvāsā”ti pakkhipitabbaṃ.

450. Regarding the verses—'in a faction, harmonious, faction-minded,' and so on—are the verses previously stated. Here, however, there is a distinction: 'does' here should be taken to mean 'performs the Pavāraṇā.' In the third verse, after removing 'does not recite the Pātimokkha,' the phrase 'should not perform the Pavāraṇā' should be inserted. In the fourth verse, after removing 'on the non-Uposatha day' and the connected verse structure, 'nor to perform the Pavāraṇā, that Pavāraṇā is permissible' should be inserted. In the fifth verse, after removing 'those residing for the established Uposatha,' 'those residing for the established Pavāraṇā' should be inserted.

451. Saṅghamhi pavāritevāti purimavassūpagate saṅghamhi pavārite eva. Pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kareyyāti na ekasmiṃ uposathagge dve ñattiyo ṭhapetabbāti adhippāyo. Pacchimikāya upagantvā apariniṭṭhitavasso avuttho. Anupāgatoti vassaṃ anupāgato. Ayametthādhippāyo – purimikāya vassaṃ upagatā pañca vā atirekā vā pacchimikāya upagatā tehi samā vā ūnatarā vā purimikāya vā upagatehi pacchimikāya upagatā thokatarā ceva honti, saṅghappavāraṇāya gaṇaṃ pūrenti saṅghappavāraṇāvasena ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā, atha ca ubhopi ekato hutvā saṅghaṃ na pūrenti, gaṇaṃ pana pūrenti, gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavāretabbaṃ, pacchā tesaṃ santike pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Yadi pana purimikāya eko, pacchimikāya eko, ekena ekassa santike pavāretabbaṃ, ekena pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Sace purimehi vassūpagatehi pacchā vassūpagatā ekenapi adhikā saṅghaṃ pūrenti, paṭhamaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitvā pacchā tesaṃ santike pavāretabbanti. Gaṇepi eseva nayo. Evamuparipi yathāyogaṃ cintanīyaṃ.

451. 'When the Saṅgha has performed the invitation'—this refers to when the Saṅgha that entered the rains earlier has already performed the invitation. 'Should perform the purity Uposatha'—the meaning is that two motions should not be introduced in a single Uposatha hall. Those who entered the later rains are those who have not completed the rains and have not resided. 'Not entered' means one who has not entered the rains. The meaning here is this: when those who entered the earlier rains are five or more, and those who entered the later rains are equal in number or fewer than them; or, when those who entered the later rains are fewer than those who entered the earlier rains, and they complete a quorum for a Saṅgha’s Pavāraṇā, having established a motion as for a Saṅgha’s Pavāraṇā; yet if both groups together do not complete a Saṅgha, but do complete a quorum, then the Pavāraṇā should be performed after establishing a quorum-motion. Later, the purity Uposatha should be performed in their presence. But if one entered the earlier rains and one entered the later rains, one should perform the Pavāraṇā in the other’s presence, and one should perform the purity Uposatha. If those who entered the rains later, together with those who entered earlier, are more numerous by even one and complete a Saṅgha, first the Pātimokkha should be recited, and then the Pavāraṇā should be performed in their presence. The same method applies to a quorum. Thus, this should be considered further as is appropriate.

452. Cātumāsiniyāti [M 0.0429] aparakattikapuṇṇamāyaṃ. Saṅghenāti paṭhamaṃ vassūpagatena saṅghena. Vutthā vassā yehi te vutthavassā, pacchimavassūpagatā. Sace appatarā siyunti iminā yadi adhikatarā vā samasamā vā honti, pavāraṇāñattiṃ ṭhapetvā pacchimavassūpagatehi paṭhamaṃ pavārite pacchā itarehi pārisuddhiuposatho kātabboti dīpetīti.

452. 'On the Cātumāsinī' means on the full moon of the later Kattika. 'By the Saṅgha'—that is, by the Saṅgha that first entered the rains. 'Those whose rains-residence is completed'—those whose rains-residence is completed are those who undertook the later rains. 'If they are fewer'—this indicates that if they are more or equal, then after the motion for Pavāraṇā has been established and the Pavāraṇā has first been performed by those who undertook the later rains, afterwards the purity Uposatha should be performed by the others.

Pavāraṇāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Pavāraṇā is concluded.

46. Saṃvaraniddesavaṇṇanā

46. Commentary on the Exposition of Restraint

453. Saṃvaraṇaṃ cakkhudvārādīnaṃ satikavāṭena pidahanaṃ saṃvaro. Tattha kiñcāpi cakkhundriye saṃvaro natthi, na hi cakkhupasādaṃ nissāya sati uppajjati, neva bhavaṅgasamaye āvajjanādīnaṃ [V 0.0359] aññatarasamaye, javanakkhaṇe pana uppajjatīti tadā saṃvaro hoti, evaṃ honte pana so cakkhudvārādīnaṃ saṃvaroti vuccati. Cakkhusotādibhedehīti cakkhu ca sotañca, tāni ādi yesaṃ, teva bhedā cāti samāso, tehi dvārehi. Abhijjhādippavattiyā accantopakārakattā karaṇatthe cettha tatiyā. Etena cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyamanasaṅkhātāni dvārāni vuttāni. Rūpasaddādigocareti rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbadhammasaṅkhāte visaye. Abhijjhādomanassādippavattinti ettha parasampattiṃ abhimukhaṃ jhāyatīti abhijjhā, balavataṇhā. Ādi-saddena micchādiṭṭhiādayo aneke akusalā dhammā saṅgahitā.

453. Restraint is the closing of the doors of the eye, etc., with the bolt of mindfulness. Herein, although there is no restraint at the eye faculty—since mindfulness does not arise dependent on the eye sensitivity, neither during the moment of life-continuum nor during any of the moments of adverting, etc., but arises only at the moment of impulsion—at that time, restraint occurs. Thus, it is called the restraint of the doors of the eye, etc. 'Through the divisions of the eye, ear, etc.': the eye and the ear, and those that are their beginning, these are the divisions; this is a compound meaning 'through those doors.' The instrumental case is used here in the sense of means, as it is entirely conducive to the arising of covetousness, etc. By this, the doors known as the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are indicated. 'In the sphere of visible forms, sounds, etc.': in the objects known as visible forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, and mental phenomena. 'The arising of covetousness, displeasure, etc.': here, 'covetousness' is so-called because it contemplates another’s property with longing; it is strong craving. By the word 'etc.,' many unwholesome states such as wrong view are included.

454. Sakaṃ cittaṃ kiṭṭhādiṃ duppasuṃ viya niggaṇheyyāti sambandho. Kiṭṭhanti kiṭṭhaṭṭhāne uppannaṃ sassaṃ gahitaṃ. Kiṭṭhaṃ adatīti [M 0.0430] kiṭṭhādi, taṃ. Sampajānoti sātthakasappāyagocaraasammohasaṅkhātena catusampajaññena sammā pajāno. Iminā indriyasaṃvarasīlaṃ kathitaṃ.

454. The connection is: 'One should restrain one's own mind, just as one would restrain a difficult-to-manage, crop-eating animal.' Here, 'kiṭṭha' is taken as the grain that has grown in a cultivated place. That animal is a 'crop-eater' (kiṭṭhādi) because it eats the crops (kiṭṭhaṃ). 'Clearly comprehending'—properly understanding with the fourfold clear comprehension, namely, of purpose, of suitability, of domain, and of non-delusion. By this, the virtue of sense-restraint is spoken of.

Saṃvaraniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of Restraint is concluded.

47. Suddhiniddesavaṇṇanā

47. Commentary on the Exposition of Purity

455. Desanā saṃvaro eṭṭhi paccavekkhaṇanti bhedato suddhi catubbidhāti sambandho. “Paccavekkhaṇaṃ bhedato”ti vattabbe niggahitalopo daṭṭhabbo, desanāsuddhi saṃvarasuddhi pariyeṭṭhisuddhi paccavekkhaṇasuddhīti catubbidhāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha sujjhatīti suddhi, yathādhammaṃ desanāya suddhi desanāsuddhi. Vuṭṭhānassāpi cettha desanāya eva saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Mūlāpattīnaṃ pana abhikkhutāpaṭiññāva desanāti heṭṭhā vuttā, sāvassa pārājikāpannassa visuddhi nāma hoti. Ayañhi yasmā pārājikaṃ āpanno, tasmā bhikkhubhāve ṭhatvā abhabbo jhānādīni adhigantuṃ. Bhikkhubhāvo hissa saggantarāyo ceva hoti, maggantarāyo ca. Vuttañhetaṃ –

455. The connection is: “Purification is fourfold by division: confession, restraint, seeking, and reflection.” Though it should be said, “Paccavekkhaṇaṃ bhedato,” the elision of the niggahita should be understood. Thus, it is said to be fourfold: purification by confession, purification by restraint, purification by seeking, and purification by reflection. Herein, suddhi means becoming pure; purification by confession is becoming pure through confession according to the Dhamma. Here, emergence should also be included in confession. However, for root offenses, the declaration of not being a bhikkhu is the confession, as stated below. For one who has committed a pārājika offense, that itself is what is called purification. For since he has committed a pārājika, remaining in the state of a bhikkhu, he is incapable of attaining jhāna and so on. Indeed, the state of a bhikkhu becomes an obstacle to heaven and an obstacle to the path for him. As it is said:

“Sāmaññaṃ dupparāmaṭṭhaṃ, nirayāyūpakaḍḍhatī”ti. (dha. pa. 311);
