However, according to the stated characteristics, even mixed or heaped earth, or even fine dust settled on a flat rock, if it becomes wet even once when it rains, after four months have passed, that wet place is designated as heaped earth. The connection is: ‘If a bhikkhu destroys plant life, a Pācittiya offense is incurred.’ Here, ‘plant life’ (bhūtagāma) is an etymological compound: ‘beings’ (bhūtā) are so-called because they exist or have existed; they are born and grow, or have been born and have grown. ‘Mass’ (gāma) means a collection. Thus, ‘bhūtagāma’ means a mass of beings, or simply beings as a mass. This term applies to established green things, such as grass, trees, and so on. ‘Destroys’ means to cut, break, or do similar actions.

36. Yo bhikkhu saṅghikaṃ mañcādiṃ ajjhokāse santharaṇādikaṃ katvā āpucchanādikaṃ akatvā yāti, tassa pācitti siyāti attho. Tattha saṅghikanti saṅghassa santakaṃ. Mañcādinti ettha ādi-saddena pīṭhabhisikocchādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Santharaṇādikanti santharaṇādiṃ katvā vā kārāpetvā vā. Āpucchanādikanti āpucchanaṃ vā uddharaṇaṃ vā uddharāpanaṃ vāti attho. Yātīti gacchati.

36. The meaning is that if a bhikkhu, having set out a Sangha-owned bed or other such item outdoors, departs without asking leave or putting it away, a Pācittiya offense is incurred. Here, ‘Sangha-owned’ means belonging to the Sangha. By ‘bed, etc.’ is included chairs, cushions, stuffed chairs, and so on. By ‘having set out’ is meant having spread it out or having had it spread out. The meaning of ‘without asking leave or putting it away’ is without asking leave, or removing it, or having it removed. By ‘departs’ is meant goes away.

37. Yo bhikkhu saṅghikāvasathe seyyaṃ santharaṇādikaṃ katvā āpucchanādikaṃ akatvā yāti, tassa bhikkhuno pācitti siyāti attho. Tattha saṅghikāvasatheti saṅghassa santake āvasathe vihāre gabbhe vā aññasmiṃ vā sabbaparicchinne guttasenāsane. Seyyanti bhisi cimilikā pāvuraṇaṃ uttarattharaṇaṃ bhūmattharaṇaṃ taṭṭikā cammakkhaṇḍaṃ nisīdanaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ tiṇasanthāro [V 0.0406] paṇṇasanthāroti evamādikaṃ. Santharaṇādikanti tesu yena kenaci attharaṇādikaṃ katvā vā kārāpetvā vā.

37. The meaning is that if a bhikkhu, having set out bedding in a Sangha dwelling, departs without asking leave or having the bedding put away, a Pācittiya offense is incurred for that bhikkhu. Here, ‘a Sangha dwelling’ means a dwelling belonging to the Sangha: a monastery, an inner chamber, or any other completely enclosed and protected lodging. ‘Bedding’ means a mattress, quilt, cloak, upper covering, ground covering, mat, piece of hide, sitting cloth, rug, grass spread, leaf spread, and so on. ‘Having set out’ means having spread out or having had spread out any of those items.

38-9. Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ toyaṃ paribhuñjaye, tassa bhikkhuno pācitti siyāti yojanā. Tattha jānaṃ [M 0.0482] sappāṇakanti “sappāṇakamida”nti disvā vā sutvā vā yena kenaci ākārena jānanto. Toyanti udakaṃ. Paribhuñjayeti paribhuñjeyya. Yo bhikkhu pārivattakaṃ ṭhapetvā aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ deti, tassa bhikkhuno pācitti siyā. Cīvarappaṭiggahaṇasikkhāpade bhikkhu paṭiggāhako idha bhikkhunī, ayaṃ viseso. Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbatopi tassa bhikkhuno pācitti siyāti attho. Cīvaranti nivāsanapārupanūpagaṃ. Sibbatoti sayaṃ sibbantassa sūciṃ pavesetvā nīharaṇe payogagaṇanāya pācitti. Sibbāpentassa pana “sibbā”ti vutto sacepi sabbaṃ sūcikammaṃ niṭṭhāpesi, ekameva pācitti, āṇattassa payogagaṇanāya pācitti hoti. Pavāretvāna atirittaṃ akāretvā bhuñjato pācitti siyāti attho. Tatrāyaṃ vinicchayo – odano sattu kummāso maccho maṃsanti pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññataraṃ sāsapamattampi ajjhoharitvā bhojanaṃ paṭikkhepaṃ katvā aññena iriyāpathena “alametaṃ sabba”nti atirittaṃ akāretvā paribhuñjato pācitti hotīti.

38-39. The construction is as follows: should a bhikkhu knowingly consume water containing living beings, a Pācittiya offense is incurred for that bhikkhu. Here, ‘knowingly containing living beings’ means knowing in any way, whether by seeing or hearing, that ‘this contains living beings.’ ‘Toya’ means water. ‘Paribhuñjaye’ means one should consume. Should a bhikkhu, except by way of exchange, give a robe to an unrelated bhikkhunī, a Pācittiya offense is incurred for that bhikkhu. In the training rule on receiving a robe, the bhikkhu is the recipient, whereas here it is the bhikkhunī; this is the difference. The meaning is that even for a bhikkhu who sews a robe for an unrelated bhikkhunī, a Pācittiya offense is incurred. ‘Robe’ refers to that which is suitable for an under-robe or an upper-robe. Regarding ‘sewing’: for one sewing himself, there is a Pācittiya for each effort of inserting and removing the needle. But for one who has someone else sew it, if the person told 'sew!' completes all the needlework, there is only one Pācittiya offense for the one who gave the order; for the one who was commanded, a Pācittiya offense is incurred for each effort. The meaning is that for one who eats after having been formally satisfied, without having the food made into a leftover, a Pācittiya offense is incurred. Here is the clarification: having swallowed even a mustard-seed's amount of any of the five kinds of food—cooked rice, flour, barley gruel, fish, or meat—and then having refused more food, saying, ‘Enough of all this,’ and having changed one's posture, if one then consumes more without having it made into a leftover, a Pācittiya offense is committed.

40. Yo bhikkhu āsādanāpekkho bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ bhikkhuṃ “handa, bhikkhu, khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti anatirittena pavāreti, bhojane bhutte tassa pācittiyaṃ udīritanti attho. Tattha āsādanāpekkhoti āsādanaṃ codanaṃ maṅkukaraṇabhāvaṃ apekkhamāno.

40. The meaning is that if a bhikkhu, seeking an occasion to find fault, invites a bhikkhu who has finished eating and declined further food, saying, ‘Come, bhikkhu, eat or chew,’ with what is not a leftover, then when the food is consumed, a Pācittiya offense is declared for him. Here, ‘seeking an occasion to find fault’ means expecting an occasion for accusation or disparagement.

41-2. Yo bhikkhu sannidhibhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya, tassa bhikkhuno pācitti siyāti attho. Tattha sannidhibhojananti paṭiggahetvā ekarattaṃ vītināmitabhojanaṃ. Vikāle yāvakālikaṃ bhuñjato vāpi pācitti siyāti yojanā. Tattha vikāleti vigatakāle, majjhanhikātikkamato paṭṭhāya [M 0.0483] yāva aruṇuggamanāti attho. Yāvakālikanti vanamūlaphalādikaṃ āmisabhojanaṃ. Agilāno bhikkhu paṇītakaṃ sappibhattādikampi viññāpetvāna bhuñjeyya, tassa bhikkhuno pācitti siyāti yojanā. Tattha agilānoti kallako. Paṇītakanti sappitelamadhuphāṇitamacchamaṃsakhīradadhisaṅkhātehi saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sattadhaññanibbattaṃ paṇītabhojanaṃ[V 0.0407]. Yo bhikkhu dantakaṭṭhodakaṃ vajjetvā appaṭiggahitakaṃ bhuñjeyya, pācitti siyāti attho. Tattha appaṭiggahitanti kāyena vā kāyappaṭibaddhena vā gaṇhantassa hatthapāse ṭhatvā kāyakāyappaṭibaddhanissaggiyānaṃ aññatarena na dinnaṃ appaṭiggahitaṃ nāma.

41-2. Should a bhikkhu consume stored-up food, that bhikkhu commits an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning. Herein, 'stored-up food' means food received and kept overnight. Even if one consumes food allowable for a limited time at the wrong time, it entails an offense entailing confession—this is the explanation. Herein, 'at the wrong time' means after the proper time, starting from midday until dawn—this is the meaning. 'Food allowable for a limited time' refers to forest roots, fruits, and similar material food. If a healthy bhikkhu requests and consumes choice food like ghee rice, etc., that bhikkhu commits an offense entailing confession—this is the explanation. Herein, 'healthy' means well. 'Choice' refers to choice food mixed with ghee, oil, honey, molasses, fish, meat, milk, or curd, or produced from the seven kinds of grain. Should a bhikkhu consume anything unaccepted, except tooth-wood and water, he commits an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning. Herein, 'unaccepted' is so-called when something has not been given by one of the means—by body or by what is connected to the body—while standing within hand's reach of the one receiving it.

43. Yo bhikkhu titthiyassa sahatthato kiñci bhuñjitabbaṃ dadeyya, tassa pācitti siyāti sambandho. Tattha titthiyassāti aññatitthiyassa. Kiñci bhuñjitabbanti yaṃ kiñci bhojanīyaṃ. Sahatthatoti sahatthā. Yo bhikkhu mātugāmena ekato raho nisajjaṃ kappeyya, tassa pācitti siyāti sambandho. Tattha rahoti paṭicchanne. Kappeti kappeyya. Ekatoti saddhiṃ.

43. Should a bhikkhu give anything edible to a member of another sect with his own hand, he commits an offense entailing confession—this is the connection. Herein, 'member of another sect' means a follower of another sect. 'Anything edible' refers to any kind of food. 'With his own hand' means with his own hand. Should a bhikkhu arrange to sit privately together with a woman, he commits an offense entailing confession—this is the connection. Herein, 'privately' means in a hidden place. 'Arrange' means he should arrange. 'Together' means with her.

44. Surāmerayapānepīti ettha piṭṭhādīhi kataṃ majjaṃ surā. Pupphādīhi kato āsavo merayaṃ. Yo bhikkhu tadubhayampi bījato paṭṭhāya kusaggenāpi pivati, tassa tappānapaccayā pācittiyaṃ udīritanti attho. Aṅgulipatodake cāpīti aṅgulīhi upakacchakādīnaṃ ghaṭṭanapaccayā pācitti siyāti attho. Hasadhammepi codaketi uparigopphake udake hasadhamme kīḷānimittaṃ tassa pācitti siyāti attho.

44. Concerning the drinking of intoxicants—here, liquor made from flour, etc., is surā. Fermented liquor made from flowers, etc., is meraya. Should a bhikkhu drink even a drop of either of these, he commits an offense entailing confession on account of that drinking—this is the meaning. And concerning tickling with the fingers—if a bhikkhu causes a sensation by rubbing the armpits, etc., with his fingers, he commits an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning. And concerning playing in the water—if a bhikkhu, for the sake of amusement, plays in water above the ankles, he commits an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning.

45. Anādarepi pācittīti puggalassa vā dhammassa vā anādarakaraṇepi pācitti siyāti attho. Yo bhikkhu upasampannena [M 0.0484] paññattena vuccamāno tassa vā vacanaṃ akattukāmatāya, taṃ vā dhammaṃ asikkhitukāmatāya anādariyaṃ karoti, tassa tasmiṃ anādariye pācitti siyāti attho. Bhayānakaṃ kathaṃ katvā vā bhayānakaṃ rūpaṃ dassetvā vā bhikkhuṃ bhīsayatopi pācitti siyāti attho.

45. Even in disrespect, there is an offense entailing confession—this means that even in an act of disrespect toward a person or the Dhamma, there is an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning. Should a bhikkhu, when being addressed regarding what has been prescribed by one who is fully ordained, show disrespect out of unwillingness to comply with that speech or unwillingness to train in that Dhamma, he commits an offense entailing confession for that disrespect—this is the meaning. Even if a bhikkhu frightens another bhikkhu by telling a frightening story or showing a frightening sight, there is an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning.

46. Yo bhikkhu agilāno kiñci paccayaṃ ṭhapetvā jotiṃ jaleyya vā jalāpeyya vā, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti sambandho. Tattha kiñci paccayanti padīpujjalanaṃ vā pattapacanādīsu jotikaraṇaṃ vāti evarūpaṃ paccayaṃ ṭhapetvā. Jotinti aggiṃ.

46. If a bhikkhu who is not ill, without any reason, kindles a fire or has it kindled, there is an offense entailing confession for him—this is the connection. Herein, 'without any reason' means apart from such reasons as lighting a lamp or making a fire for cooking in a bowl, etc. 'A fire' means fire.

47-8. Kappabinduṃ anādāya navacīvarabhogino navaṃ cīvaraṃ bhuñjantassa pācitti siyāti attho. Kappabindunti morakkhimaṇḍalamaṅgulapiṭṭhīnaṃ aññatarappamāṇaṃ kappabinduṃ. Anādāyāti anādiyitvā. Bhikkhuno cīvarādikaṃ parikkhāraṃ apanetvā nidhentassa vā nidhāpentassa [V 0.0408] vā hasāpekkhassa bhikkhuno pācitti siyāti attho. Cīvarādikanti ādi-saddena pattanisīdanasūcigharakāyabandhanādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Nidhentassāti nidahantassa. Hasāpekkhassāti hasādhippāyassa. Jānaṃ pāṇaṃ hane bhikkhu, tiracchānagatampi cāti yo bhikkhu “pāṇo”ti jānanto tiracchānagataṃ pāṇaṃ khuddakampi mahantampi haneyya, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti attho.

47-8. The meaning is: For a bhikkhu who uses a new robe without applying the prescribed mark, there is an offense entailing confession. 'The prescribed mark' refers to a mark the size of a peacock's eye-circle or the back of a fingernail. 'Without applying' means without having applied it. If a bhikkhu, with the intention of jesting, takes away or has someone take away another bhikkhu’s robe or other requisites and hides them, there is an offense entailing confession for him—this is the meaning. 'Robe or other requisites' includes, by the word 'other,' items such as bowls, sitting cloths, needle cases, and waistbands. 'Hides' means hiding. 'With the intention of jesting' means with the intention of joking. If a bhikkhu, knowingly, kills a living being—even an animal—whether small or large, there is an offense entailing confession for him—this is the meaning.

49. Chādetukāmo chādeti, duṭṭhullaṃ bhikkhunopi cāti yo bhikkhu bhikkhuno duṭṭhullasaṅkhātaṃ saṅghādisesaṃ chādetukāmo hutvā chādeti, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti attho. Itthiyā saha saṃvidhāya gāmantaragatassa bhikkhuno pācittiyaṃ siyāti yojanā.

49. The meaning is: If a bhikkhu, wishing to conceal, conceals a saṅghādisesa offense, which is designated a grave offense, of another bhikkhu, there is an offense entailing confession for him. The application is: For a bhikkhu who, by arrangement with a woman, goes to another village, there is an offense entailing confession.

50. Bhikkhuṃ [M 0.0485] vā pahareyyāthāti yo bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ pahareyya, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti yojanā. Talasattikamuggireti yo bhikkhu paharaṇākāraṃ dassento kāyaṃ vā kāyappaṭibaddhaṃ vā uggireyya, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti attho. Codeyya vā codāpeyya, bhikkhuṃ amūlakena cāti yo bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena codeyya vā codāpeyya vā, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti attho. Tattha amūlakenāti diṭṭhādimūlavirahitena.

50. The application is: If a bhikkhu strikes another bhikkhu, there is an offense entailing confession. 'Raises a palm or a weapon' means if a bhikkhu, while showing the manner of striking, raises his body or something connected with his body, there is an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning. If a bhikkhu accuses or has another accuse a bhikkhu of a saṅghādisesa offense without foundation, there is an offense entailing confession—this is the meaning. Herein, 'without foundation' means lacking a basis such as having seen, etc.

51. Kukkuccuppādane cāpīti “ūnavīsativasso tvaṃ maññe”tiādīni bhaṇanto kukkuccaṃ uppādeyya, tassa kukkuccuppādanapaccayā pācittiyaṃ hoti. Yo bhikkhu bhaṇḍanatthāya bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ vacanaṃ sotuṃ upassutiṃ yāti, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti sambandho. Tattha bhaṇḍanatthāyāti kalahatthāya. Bhaṇḍanajātānanti kalahajātānaṃ. Upassutinti sutisamīpaṃ.

51. 'And also in creating anxiety' means if one, saying, 'I think you must be under twenty years old,' etc., creates anxiety, there is an offense entailing confession because of that act of creating anxiety. If a bhikkhu, for the purpose of quarreling, goes to eavesdrop on the words of those engaged in a quarrel, there is an offense entailing confession for him—this is the connection. Herein, 'for the purpose of quarreling' means for the sake of dispute. 'Of those engaged in a quarrel' means of those involved in conflict. 'To eavesdrop' means to a place near hearing.

52. Yo bhikkhu saṅghassa pariṇāmitaṃ yaṃ lābhaṃ, taṃ parapuggalassa nāmeti, tassa pācittiyaṃ siyāti sambandho. Tattha nāmetīti pariṇāmeti. Pucchaṃ akatvāti “vikāle gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchāmī”ti vā “gāmaṃ pavisissāmī”ti vā anāpucchitvā. Santabhikkhunti antoupacārasīmāya dassanūpacāre bhikkhuṃ disvā yaṃ sakkā hoti pakativacanena āpucchituṃ, tādisaṃ vijjamānaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Gāmassāti gāmaṃ, kammatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Gateti sampadānatthe bhummavacanaṃ, gatassāti attho. Santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchitvā vikāle gāmaṃ gatassa bhikkhuno pācittiyaṃ siyāti attho. Sesaṃ uttānamevāti.

52. If a bhikkhu redirects any gain that has been designated for the Sangha to another individual, there is an offense entailing confession for him—this is the connection. Herein, 'redirects' means to assign. 'Without asking' means not having asked permission by saying, 'I ask leave to enter the village at an improper time,' or 'I will enter the village.' 'A bhikkhu being present' refers to seeing a bhikkhu within the inner boundary or within sight, such a present bhikkhu who can be asked with a normal utterance. The genitive form for 'village' (gāmassa) is used here for the accusative (gāmaṃ), in the sense of the object. The locative 'gone' (gate) is used in the dative sense; the meaning is 'to one who has gone' (gatassa). The meaning is that if a bhikkhu goes to the village at an improper time without asking a present bhikkhu, there is an offense entailing confession for him. The rest is clear.

Pācittiyaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Pācittiya Rules is concluded.

5. Pakiṇṇakaniddesavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Miscellaneous Section

53. Idāni [M 0.0486][V 0.0409] pakiṇṇakaṃ dassetuṃ “saṅghika”ntyādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yo bhikkhu issaro hutvā saṅghikaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ aññassa deti, tassa thullaccayaṃ siyā. Theyyāya aññassa deti, yathāvatthu pārājikādi siyā, dukkaṭavatthu dukkaṭaṃ, thullaccayavatthu thullaccayaṃ, pārājikavatthu pārājikaṃ siyāti vuttaṃ hoti.

53. Now, to explain the miscellaneous matters, the section beginning with “belonging to the Saṅgha” is commenced. Here, if a bhikkhu, being in charge, gives a heavy item belonging to the Saṅgha to another, he incurs a grave offense (thullaccaya). If he gives it to another with the intention of theft, then, depending on the object, it would be a pārājika or the like; if the object warrants a dukkaṭa, it is a dukkaṭa; if it warrants a thullaccaya, it is a thullaccaya; if it warrants a pārājika, it is a pārājika—this is what is meant.

54. Kusādimayacīrānīti ettha ādi-saddo vākaphalakaṃ saṅgaṇhāti, kusamayacīraṃ vākamayacīraṃ phalakamayacīranti. Tattha kuse ganthetvā katacīraṃ kusamayacīraṃ. Vākamayacīraṃ nāma tāpasānaṃ vakkalaṃ. Phalakamayacīraṃ nāma phalakasaṇṭhānāni phalakāni sibbetvā katacīraṃ. Kambalaṃ kesavālajanti kesajaṃ kambalaṃ vālajaṃ kambalaṃ, kesakambalaṃ vālakambalanti attho. Kesehi tante vāyitvā katakambalaṃ kesakambalaṃ. Camarivālehi vāyitvā katakambalaṃ vālakambalaṃ. Samayaṃ vināti naṭṭhacīvarakālaṃ ṭhapetvā. Dhārayato dhārayantassa. Lūkapakkhājinakkhipanti ulūkapakkhiajinakkhipaṃ. Tattha ulūkapakkhīti ulūkasakuṇapakkhehi katanivāsanaṃ. Ajinakkhipanti salomaṃ sakhuraṃ ajinamigacammaṃ. Naṭṭhacīvarakālaṃ ṭhapetvā imesu sattasu vatthūsu yaṃ kiñci dhārayato thullaccayaṃ siyāti attho.

54. Regarding 'robes made of kusa grass, etc.,' here the word 'etc.' includes bark and planks, meaning a robe made of kusa grass, a robe made of bark, and a robe made of planks. Among these, a robe made by binding kusa grass is a kusa-grass robe. A bark robe refers to the bark clothing of ascetics. A plank robe refers to a robe made by sewing together plank-shaped pieces. Regarding 'a blanket made of hair or animal fur,' it means a blanket made from hair or a blanket made from animal fur, that is, a hair blanket or a fur blanket. A hair blanket is a blanket woven from hair threads. A fur blanket is a blanket woven from the fur of a chamara yak. Regarding 'without a proper reason' (samayaṃ vinā), it means excluding the time when a robe is lost. 'For one who wears it' means for one who is wearing it. Regarding 'an owl-feather cloak or a hide garment,' it refers to an owl-feather garment or a hide garment. Here, an owl-feather garment is a lower garment made from the feathers of an owl. A hide garment is the skin of an animal, with hair and hooves. Excluding the time when a robe is lost, for one who wears any of these seven items, there is a grave offense (thullaccaya)—this is the meaning.

55. Satthakena kattabbaṃ kammaṃ satthakammaṃ, tasmiṃ satthakamme. Vatthimhi kattabbaṃ kammaṃ vatthikammaṃ, tasmiṃ vatthikamme. Saṃ nimittanti attano aṅgajātaṃ. Taṃ chindato thullaccayaṃ siyāti sambandho. Maṃsādibhojaneti ettha ādi-saddo aṭṭhilohitacammalomāni saṅgaṇhāti. Tasmā manussānaṃ maṃsaaṭṭhilohitacammalomabhojanapaccayā thullaccayaṃ siyāti attho.

55. Work to be done with a knife (satthaka) is knife-work; in that knife-work. Work to be done on the bladder (vatthi) is bladder-work; in that bladder-work. 'One's own sign' (saṃ nimittaṃ) refers to one’s own genitals. For cutting that, there is a grave offense (thullaccaya)—this is the connection. Regarding 'eating meat, etc.,' here the word 'etc.' includes bones, blood, skin, and hair. Therefore, on account of consuming the meat, bones, blood, skin, or hair of humans, there is a grave offense (thullaccaya)—this is the meaning.

56. Kadalerakakkadussānīti [M 0.0487] ettha kadalierakaakkavākehi katāni vatthāni dhārayantassa dukkaṭaṃ. Potthakanti makacivākehi kataṃ potthakadussaṃ. Sabbapītādikanti ettha ādi-saddena sabbalohitakasabbakaṇhakasabbamañjeṭṭhikaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Tattha sabbameva nīlakaṃ sabbanīlakaṃ. Evaṃ sesesupi. Nīlaṃ ummārapupphavaṇṇaṃ. Pītaṃ kaṇikārapupphavaṇṇaṃ. Lohitaṃ jayasumanapupphavaṇṇaṃ. Kaṇhakaṃ addāriṭṭhakavaṇṇaṃ. Mañjeṭṭhikaṃ lākhārasavaṇṇaṃ. Imesu aṭṭhasu vatthūsu yaṃ kiñci dhārayantassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho.

56. Regarding 'garments of kadali, eraka, and akka,' for one wearing garments made from kadali, eraka, or akka fibers, there is a dukkaṭa offense. 'Potthaka' refers to a potthaka cloth made of makaci fibers. Regarding 'all yellow, etc.,' here the word 'etc.' includes all red, all black, and all madder-red. Among these, 'all blue' means entirely blue. Similarly for the rest. Blue is the color of the ummārapuppha flower. Yellow is the color of the kaṇikāra flower. Red is the color of the jayasumana flower. Black is the color of the addāriṭṭhaka. Madder-red is the color of lac-dye. For one wearing any of these eight types of cloth, there is a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning.

57-8. Hatthissuragasoṇānanti [V 0.0410] hatthiassauragasoṇānaṃ maṃsaṃ aṭṭhirudhiracammalomāni. Sīhabyagghacchadīpinanti sīhabyagghaacchadīpīnaṃ maṃsādīni. Taracchassa ca maṃsādiṃ uddissakatamaṃsañca anāpucchitamaṃsañca bhuñjato dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Dakatitthādikanti ettha ādi-saddo vaccapassāvakuṭiyo saṅgaṇhāti. Tena yātānupubbaṃ āgatappaṭipāṭiṃ hitvāna vajjetvā nahānatitthañca vaccakuṭiñca passāvakuṭiñca vaje vajeyya gaccheyya, dukkaṭaṃ tassa siyāti attho.

57-8. Regarding 'of the elephant, horse, serpent, and dog,' it refers to the flesh, bones, blood, skin, and hair of elephants, horses, serpents, and dogs. Regarding 'of the lion, tiger, bear, and leopard,' it refers to the flesh, etc., of lions, tigers, bears, and leopards. For one who eats the flesh, etc., of a hyena (taraccha), or meat prepared on purpose for him, or meat taken without asking, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Regarding 'a bathing place, etc.,' here the word 'etc.' includes toilets and urinals. Therefore, abandoning the established order of arrival, if one were to go to a bathing place, a toilet, or a urinal, for him there would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning.

59. Sahasāti vegasā vegena. Vubbhajitvānāti antaravāsakaṃ dūratova ukkhipitvā, va-kāro sandhivasenāgato. Paviseti paviseyya. Vaccapassāvakuṭikanti vaccakuṭikaṃ passāvakuṭikaṃ. Viseti paviseyya. Yo bhikkhu vaccapassāvakuṭikaṃ sahasā paviseyya vā nikkhameyya vā, ubbhajitvā vā paviseyya vā nikkhameyya vā, ukkāsikaṃ vajjetvā taṃ paviseyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti yojanā.

59. ‘Hastily’ (sahasā) means quickly, with speed. ‘Having lifted up’ (vubbhajitvāna) means tossing the lower robe from a distance—the ‘va’ is inserted by means of euphony. ‘Enters’ (paviseti) means one should enter. ‘Latrine or urinal’ (vaccapassāvakuṭikaṃ) means a latrine and a urinal. ‘Enters’ (viseti) means one should enter. The construction is as follows: If a bhikkhu should enter or exit a latrine or urinal hastily, or should enter or exit after lifting up his robe, or should enter it without making a cough, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense.

60. Nitthunanto vaccaṃ kareyya dantakaṭṭhañca khādanto, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Vaccapassāvadoṇīnaṃ bahi vaccādikaṃ vaccapassāvaṃ kareyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā.

60. If one were to defecate while groaning or while chewing a tooth-stick, for him there would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning. If one were to defecate or urinate outside the latrine or urine receptacles, for him there would be a dukkaṭa offense.

61. Kharena [M 0.0488] cāvalekheyyāti phālitakaṭṭhena vā pharusena vā gaṇṭhikena vā pūtikaṭṭhena vā susirena vā avalekheyyāti attho. Kaṭṭhanti avalekhanakaṭṭhaṃ. Kūpaketi vaccakūpake. Ūhatañcāti gūthamakkhitañca. Na dhoveyyāti attanā vā na dhoveyya parena vā na dhovāpeyya. Uklāpañcāti kacavarañca. Na sodhayena sammajjeyya.

61. Regarding 'one should scrape with a rough object' (kharena cāvalekheyya), it means one should scrape with a split piece of wood, or a rough piece, or a knotty piece, or a rotten piece, or a perforated piece. 'Wood' (kaṭṭhaṃ) refers to a scraping-stick. 'In the pit' (kūpake) means in the privy pit. 'And soiled' (ūhatañca) means smeared with excrement. 'Should not wash' (na dhoveyya) means one should not wash it oneself nor have another wash it. 'And rubbish' (uklāpañca) means sweepings. One should not clean or sweep.

62. Capucapūti saddaṃ katvā udakakiccaṃ karontassa ācamantassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Anajjhiṭṭhovāti anāṇattoyeva. Therenāti saṅghattherena. Pātimokkhanti pātimokkhuddesaṃ. Uddise uddiseyya, dukkaṭaṃ siyā.

62. For one making a 'capucapu' sound while performing his water duty, that is, while rinsing his mouth, there is a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning. 'Unrequested' (anajjhiṭṭho) means uninstructed. 'By an elder' (therena) means by the elder of the Saṅgha. 'The Pātimokkha' (pātimokkhaṃ) means the recitation of the Pātimokkha. If one should recite it (uddise uddiseyya), there is a dukkaṭa offense.

63. Anāpucchāya pañhassa kathane, anāpucchāya pañhassa vissajjane, anāpucchāya sajjhāyakaraṇe, anāpucchāya padīpajālane, anāpucchāya padīpavijjhāpaneti imesu catūsu paccayesu tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā.

63. For speaking on a question without being asked, for answering a question without being asked, for making a recitation without being asked, for lighting a lamp without being asked, and for extinguishing a lamp without being asked—in these four instances, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense.

64. Anāpucchā [V 0.0411] vātapānakavāṭāni vivareyya vā thakeyya vā, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Vandanādinti ettha ādi-saddo vandāpanaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Yo bhikkhu naggo vandanaṃ kareyya, vandāpanaṃ kareyya, gamanaṃ kareyya, bhojanaṃ kareyya, pivanaṃ kareyya, khādanaṃ kareyya, gahaṇaṃ kareyya, dānaṃ kareyya, tassa sabbattha dukkaṭanti sambandho.

64. If one should open or close windows or doors without asking, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection. Regarding 'paying respects, etc.,' here the word 'etc.' includes causing others to pay respects. The connection is as follows: If a bhikkhu, being naked, should pay respects, cause others to pay respects, go, eat, drink, chew, take, or give, in all cases there is a dukkaṭa offense.

65. Tipaṭicchannakaṃ vināti “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tisso paṭicchādiyo jantāgharappaṭicchādiṃ udakappaṭicchādiṃ vatthappaṭicchādi”nti (cūḷava. 261) evaṃ vuttā tisso paṭicchādiyo samāhaṭāti “tipaṭicchādī”ti vuttaṃ. Tipaṭicchannakaṃ ṭhapetvā parikammaṃ sayaṃ kareyya, paraṃ kārāpeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho[M 0.0489]. Yo bhikkhu nahāyaṃ nahāyanto kuṭṭe vā thambhe vā tarumhi vā kāyaṃ upaghaṃseyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā.

65. Regarding 'without the three coverings' (tipaṭicchannakaṃ vinā): the three coverings are mentioned thus, 'I allow, bhikkhus, three coverings: a bathhouse covering, a water covering, and a clothing covering' (Cūḷavagga 261). These three coverings, taken together, are called 'the three coverings' (tipaṭicchādī). Excluding the case of the three coverings, if one were to attend to his body himself, or have another attend to it, for him there would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning. If a bhikkhu, while bathing, should rub his body against a wall, a post, or a tree, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense.

66. Yo bhikkhu nahāyanto kuruvindakasuttena kāyaṃ ghaṃseyya, kāyato kāyena aññamaññaṃ ghaṃseyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Yo agilāno saupāhano bahārāme bahiārāme careyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho.

66. The connection is as follows: If a bhikkhu, while bathing, should rub his body with a string of kuruvindaka powder, or should rub body against body with another, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense. The connection is as follows: If a bhikkhu who is not ill, wearing footwear, should walk about outside the monastery, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense.

67. Sabbanīlādikampi cāti ettha ādi-saddo lohitodātapītakaṇhamañjeṭṭhamahāraṅgamahānāmaraṅgarattādayo upāhanāyo saṅgaṇhāti. Yo bhikkhu sabbanīlasabbalohitādikaṃ upāhanaṃ dhāreti, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Yo bhikkhu ratto rattacitto tadahujātāyapi itthiyā nimittaṃ passeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Yo bhikkhu bhikkhadāyiyā bhikkhadāyikāya itthiyā mukhaṃ passeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā.

67. Regarding 'all blue, etc.,' here the word 'etc.' includes the following kinds of footwear: red, white, yellow, black, madder-red, great-dye, great-name-dye, and red-dye. The connection is as follows: If a bhikkhu wears footwear that is entirely blue, entirely red, or the like, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense. If a bhikkhu, being lustful and with a lustful mind, should see the sexual organ (nimittaṃ) of a female, even one born that very day, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense. If a bhikkhu should see the face of a woman who is a giver of alms, a female alms-giver, for him there is a dukkaṭa offense.

68-9. Yo bhikkhu ujjhānasaññī hutvā aññassa bhikkhuno pattaṃ vā passeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Ādāsādimhi udakapatte attano mukhaṃ passeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Uccāsanamahāsane nisajjādiṃ nisīdanasayanādiṃ karontassa bhikkhuno dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Ukkhittānupasampannanānāsaṃvāsakādīnaṃ vandanepi dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Tattha ukkhittoti āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakoti tividhopi idhādhippeto. Anupasampannoti iminā bhikkhunisāmaṇerasāmaṇerisikkhamānapaṇḍakaitthisikkhāpaccakkhātakā [V 0.0412] gahitā. Nānāsaṃvāsakāti laddhinānāsaṃvāsakā gahitā. Ādi-saddena chinnamūlakā gahitā.

68-9. If a bhikkhu, being given to fault-finding, sees another bhikkhu’s bowl, he incurs a dukkaṭa offense. If he sees his own face in a mirror, a water vessel, or the like, he incurs a dukkaṭa offense. For a bhikkhu who sits or lies on a high seat or a large bed, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Even respecting those who have been suspended, those not fully ordained, those of different communion, and the like, incurs a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection. Here, “suspended” refers to three types: one suspended for not seeing an offense, one suspended for not making amends for an offense, and one suspended for not relinquishing a bad view—all three are intended here. “Not fully ordained” includes bhikkhunīs, male novices, female novices, probationers, eunuchs, women, and those who have renounced the training. “Different communion” refers to those of differing doctrinal communion. The term “etc.” includes those who have cut off the root.

70-71. Yo [M 0.0490] dīghāsane paṇḍakitthīhi paṇḍakena vā itthiyā vā ubhatobyañjanena vā ekato nisīdeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Adīghe āsaneti rasse āsane. Yo bhikkhu rassāsane mañce vā pīṭhe vā asamānāsanikena ekato sayeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Phalapupphādikanti ettha ādi-saddena veḷucuṇṇadantakaṭṭhamattikādayo saṅgahitā. Kulasaṅgahatthāya phalapupphādikaṃ dadato dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho.

70-71. If a bhikkhu sits on a long seat with a eunuch and a woman, or with a eunuch, or with a woman, or with a hermaphrodite, he incurs a dukkaṭa offense. “On a short seat” means on a low seat. If a bhikkhu lies down on a low seat, couch, or stool with one who does not have an equal seat, he incurs a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning. Regarding “fruits, flowers, etc.,” here the word “etc.” includes bamboo powder, tooth-sticks, clay, and the like. Giving fruits, flowers, or such things for the purpose of ingratiating himself with families incurs a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection.

72-3. Yo bhikkhu ganthimādiṃ sayaṃ kareyya, paraṃ kārāpeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Yo bhikkhu jinena vāritapaccaye paribhuñjeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Abyatto bālo yo bhikkhu ācariyupajjhāye anissāya nissayaṃ aggahetvā vaseyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Yo bhikkhu anuññātehi mātāpituādīhi puggalehi aññassa puggalassa bhesajjaṃ kareyya vā vadeyya vā, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Sāpattiko yo bhikkhu uposathappavāraṇaṃ kareyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Tattha jinena bhagavatā vāritā jinavāritā, jinavāritā ca te paccayā ceti jinavāritapaccayā, te jinavāritapaccaye. Dvemātikāappaguṇatāya abyatto.

72-3. If a bhikkhu were to make a girdle or similar item himself or have another make it, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. If a bhikkhu were to use requisites prohibited by the Victor, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. If an unskillful, foolish bhikkhu were to live without reliance, not having taken reliance on a teacher or preceptor, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. If a bhikkhu were to prepare or prescribe medicine for any person other than those permitted, such as his parents, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. If a bhikkhu with offenses were to perform the Uposatha or Pavāraṇā, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the connection. Herein, 'prohibited by the Victor' means 'prohibited by the Victor, the Blessed One.' 'Requisites prohibited by the Victor' refers to those requisites that are prohibited by the Victor. Due to his deficiency in the two matrices, he is unskillful.

74. Yo bhikkhu ābhogaṃ vā niyogaṃ vā vajjetvā dvārabandhādike ṭhāne parivattakavāṭakaṃ apidhāya divā sayeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Dvārabandhādiketi yena kenaci parikkhitte abbhokāsepi rukkhamūlepi antamaso iminā lakkhaṇena yuttaākāsaṅgaṇepi. Apidhāyāti apidahitvā. Vinābhoganti “esa dvāraṃ jaggissatī”ti ābhogaṃ ṭhapetvāti attho. Niyoganti avasaṭṭhānaṃ, attano avasaṃ bahusādhāraṇaṭṭhānaṃ ṭhapetvā. “Savaso”ti [M 0.0491] vā pāṭho, savaso hutvāti attho. Divāti divākāle.

74. If a bhikkhu, avoiding concern or assignment, were to sleep during the day in a place with a door-post or similar feature without closing it, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the connection. 'In a place with a door-post, etc.' means in any enclosed open space, even at the foot of a tree, or even in an open space possessing these characteristics. 'Without closing' means not having closed it. 'Without concern' means without having made the intention that 'this door will be guarded.' 'Assignment' means a place not under one's control; having left one's own place, a place common to many. Alternatively, the reading may be 'savaso,' meaning 'being in control.' 'During the day' means in the daytime.

75. Dhaññanti sāli vīhi yavo godhumo kaṅgu varako kudrūsakoti sattavidhaṃ dhaññaṃ. Itthirūpanti dārulohamayādiitthirūpaṃ. Ratananti muttādidasavidhaṃ ratanaṃ. Āvudhanti sattitomarādisabbāvudhabhaṇḍaṃ. Itthipasādhananti itthiyā sīsādialaṅkāraṃ. Tūriyabhaṇḍanti dhamanasaṅkhādisabbaṃ tūriyabhaṇḍaṃ. Phalarukkheti phalitarukkhe. Pubbaṇṇādikanti muggamāsādikaṃ. Ādi-saddena [V 0.0413] vākurakuminādayo gahitā. Etesu yaṃ kiñci āmaseyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho.

75. 'Grains' refers to seven kinds: fine rice, paddy, barley, wheat, millet, kaṅgu, and kudrūsaka. 'Female figurines' means figurines of women made of wood, metal, etc. 'Jewels' means ten kinds of jewels such as pearls, etc. 'Weapons' means all weaponry like spears and lances, etc. 'Women’s adornments' means ornaments for women, such as those for the head, etc. 'Musical instruments' means all musical instruments like wind instruments and conches, etc. 'Fruit trees' means fruit-bearing trees. 'Pulses, etc.' means items like mung beans and black gram. The word 'etc.' includes items like nets and traps. Handling any of these would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning.

76. Sasitthodakatelehīti yo pana madhusitthakatelena vā udakamissakatelena vā yena kenaci cikkhallena vā. Phaṇahatthaphaṇehi vāti dantamayādiphaṇena vā phaṇakiccasādhakehi hatthaṅgulīhi vā kocchena vā kesamosaṇṭhane dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Ekasmiṃ bhājane bhojananimitte dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho.

76. 'With oil with wax and water' means with oil prepared with beeswax, or with oil mixed with water, or with any greasy substance. 'With comb-hands or combs' means with a comb made of ivory or other material, or with fingers accomplishing the function of a comb, or with a brush—arranging the hair in this way is a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning. For the purpose of eating in a single receptacle, there is a dukkaṭa offense—this is the meaning.

77. Dve bhikkhū ekattharaṇā sayeyyūṃ, dve bhikkhū ekapāvuraṇā sayeyyuṃ, dve bhikkhū ekamañcake sayeyyuṃ, tesaṃ dukkaṭāni hontīti sambandho. Pamāṇato adhikaṃ vā ūnaṃ vā dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti yojanā. Tattha adhikanti aṭṭhaṅgulato adhikaṃ. Ūnanti caturaṅgulato ūnaṃ.

77. If two bhikkhus sleep on the same spread, if two bhikkhus sleep under the same covering, if two bhikkhus sleep on the same bed, they incur dukkaṭa offenses—this is the connection. If one chews a tooth-cleaner longer or shorter than the prescribed size, he incurs a dukkaṭa offense—this is the construction. Here, 'longer' means more than eight fingerbreadths. 'Shorter' means less than four fingerbreadths.

78. Yo bhikkhu naccañca gītañca vāditañca yojeti vā yojāpeti vā, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Tesaṃ naccānaṃ dassanaṃ, tesaṃ gītānaṃ savanaṃ, tesaṃ vāditānaṃ savanañca karontassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho.

78. If a bhikkhu arranges or has arranged dancing, singing, or instrumental music, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. The meaning is: for one who watches such dancing, listens to such singing, or listens to such instrumental music, that would be a dukkaṭa offense.

79. Vīhādiropimeti [M 0.0492] vīhiādīnaṃ ruhanaṭṭhāne. Bahipākārakuṭṭaketi pākārakuṭṭānaṃ bahi. Vaccādichaḍḍanādimhīti vaccapassāvasaṅkāracalakādīnaṃ chaḍḍanavissajjanapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Dīghakesādidhāraṇeti dīghakesadhāraṇe dīghanakhadhāraṇe dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho.

79. 'Planting paddy, etc.' refers to a place for growing paddy, etc. 'Outside the boundary wall' means outside the boundary walls. 'Regarding disposing of feces, etc.' means that a dukkaṭa offense arises on account of discarding or disposing of feces, urine, refuse, sweepings, etc. 'Regarding wearing long hair, etc.' means that a dukkaṭa offense arises for wearing long hair or for wearing long nails.

80. Nakhamaṭṭhakaraṇādimhīti ettha ādi-saddena rajanakaraṇaṃ gahitaṃ. Sambādhe lomahāraṇeti sambādhe upakacchakamuttakaraṇaṭṭhāne lomuddharaṇe. Saupāhano bhikkhu parikammakataṃ bhūmiṃ akkameyyāti sambandho.

80. Here, regarding 'polishing nails, etc.,' the word 'etc.' includes the application of dye. 'Removing hair in a confined space' refers to removing hair in a confined place like the armpits or the pubic region. The connection is: A bhikkhu wearing shoes should not step on prepared ground.

81. Adhotaallapādehīti yo bhikkhu adhotapādehi vā allapādehi vā saṅghikaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā akkameyya, parikammakataṃ bhittiṃ vā kāyato āmasantassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho.

81. 'With unwashed or wet feet': the meaning is, if a bhikkhu were to step on a monastic bed or chair with unwashed or wet feet, or for one touching a prepared wall with his body, that would be a dukkaṭa offense.

82-3. Saṅghāṭiyāpi [V 0.0414] pallattheti adhiṭṭhitacīvarena vihāre vā antaraghare vā pallatthikaṃ kareyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ. Dupparibhuñjeyya cīvaranti tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ dupparibhogena paribhuñjeyya. Akāyabandhanoti kāyabandhanavirahito bhikkhu gāmaṃ vajeyya gaccheyya. Yo bhikkhu vaccakaṃ uccāraṃ katvāna udake sante nācameyya udakasuddhiṃ na kareyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Samādeyya akappiyeti bhikkhuṃ vā sāmaṇerādike sesasahadhammike vā akappiye niyojeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Sabhāgāpattiyā desanārocanapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Sabhāgāti ettha vatthusabhāgatāva idhādhippetā, na āpattisabhāgatā.

82-3. 'Sitting cross-legged even with the outer robe' means that if a bhikkhu, with a determined robe, were to sit cross-legged inside a monastery or a house, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. 'Misusing the robe' means using any of the three robes with improper care. 'Without a waistband' means a bhikkhu without a waistband who goes to a village. If a bhikkhu, having defecated, and water being available, does not wash himself or does not purify himself with water, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the meaning. 'Assigning an unsuitable task' means if a bhikkhu assigns an unsuitable task to another bhikkhu, a novice, or other fellow practitioners, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the meaning. A dukkaṭa offense arises on account of the confession and announcement of an offense of the same class—this is the meaning. Here, 'same class' is intended to mean similarity of the object, not similarity of the offense.

84. Na vase vassanti yo bhikkhu vassaṃ na vaseyya na upagaccheyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Visaṃvāde suddhacitteti ettha [M 0.0493] sampadānatthe bhummavacanaṃ, paṭissavaṃ visaṃvādentassa suddhacittassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Vassaṃ vasitvā ananuññātakiccato ananuññātakiccena bhikkhuno gamane dukkaṭaṃ siyāti yojanā.

84. 'Not observing the rains retreat' means: if a bhikkhu should not observe the rains retreat, should not enter upon it, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. Regarding 'deceiving one of pure mind': here the locative case has the meaning of the dative. The meaning is: for one who breaks a promise to a person of pure mind, there is a dukkaṭa offense. Having observed the rains retreat, if a bhikkhu goes on a journey for an unpermitted reason, there is a dukkaṭa offense—this is the construction.

85. Āpadaṃ vajjetvā tarussa uddhaṃ porisamhā abhiruhaṇe dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Āpadanti antarāyaṃ. Tarussāti rukkhassa. Porisamhāti ekaporisappamāṇā majjhimassa purisassa pañcahatthā. Aparissāvano yo bhikkhu addhānaṃ gaccheyya, yo ca bhikkhu taṃ parissāvanaṃ yācato na dadeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti yojanā. Addhānanti addhayojanameva antimamaddhānaṃ.

85. Except in case of danger, climbing up a tree more than a man’s height would entail a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection. 'Danger' means an obstacle. 'Tree' means of a tree. 'A man’s height' means one man's height in measure; of an average man, five cubits. If a bhikkhu travels a distance without a filter, and if a bhikkhu does not give a filter when asked for, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the application. 'Distance' means exactly half a yojana, the minimum distance.

86. Attano ghātane dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Yo bhikkhu itthirūpādirūpaṃ kareyya vā kārāpeyya vā, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Mālādikaṃ vicittaṃ ṭhapetvā jātakādivatthuṃ sayaṃ kareyya, dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho.

86. In the case of destroying oneself, that would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection. If a bhikkhu makes or has made a female form or other such forms, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. Except for variegated things such as garlands, if he himself makes a story such as a Jātaka, that would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection.

87. Bhuñjantamuṭṭhapeti yo bhikkhu bhuñjantaṃ uṭṭhāpeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Bhattasālādīsu vuḍḍhānaṃ okāsaṃ adatvā nisīdato dukkaṭaṃ siyāti yojanā.

87. He causes one who is eating to rise: if a bhikkhu should cause a person who is eating to rise, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him. For one sitting in a dining hall or other such places without giving room to elders, there would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the application.

88. Yānānīti vayhaṃ ratho sakaṭaṃ sandamānikādīni. Kallakoti agilāno. Agilāno [V 0.0415] yo bhikkhu yānāni abhiruheyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Vade davanti keḷiṃ vadeyya, ratanattayaṃ ārabbha keḷiṃ vadeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Aññaparisāya upalālane dukkaṭaṃ hoti.

88. 'Vehicles' means palanquins, chariots, carts, sedan chairs, and so on. 'Healthy' means not ill. If a healthy bhikkhu were to mount vehicles, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the meaning. He should speak playfully: if he were to utter playful speech, if he were to utter playful speech concerning the Triple Gem, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the meaning. A dukkaṭa offense occurs for coaxing another assembly.

89. Kāyādinti ettha ādi-saddo ūrunimittaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Kāyaṃ vā ūruṃ vā nimittaṃ vā vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ na dassaye na dasseyyāti attho. Lokāyataṃ tiracchānādivijjaṃ na ca [M 0.0494] sayaṃ vāceyya, parañca na vācāpeyya. Palitaṃ gaṇheyya vā gaṇhāpeyya vā, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti yojanā.

89. 'Body, etc.'—here the term 'etc.' includes the thigh and private parts. He should not uncover and show his body, thigh, or private parts to bhikkhunīs, nor have another show them—this is the meaning. He should not himself recite Lokāyata or such base arts as animal lore, nor have another recite them. If he plucks or has another pluck grey hair, that would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection.

90-92. Yattha katthaci peḷāyaṃ pakkhipitvā bhattaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Pattahatthako yo bhikkhu vātapānaṃ vā kavāṭaṃ vā paṇāme paṇāmeyya, sodakaṃ pattaṃ uṇheyya uṇhe otāpeyya vā paṭisāmeyya vā, vodakaṃ pattaṃ atiuṇheyya atiṭhapeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Yo bhikkhu pattaṃ bhūmiyaṃ vā aṅke vā mañce vā pīṭhe vā miḍḍhante vā paribhaṇḍante vā pāde vā chatte vā ṭhapeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho. Bhūmiyanti yena kenaci anatthatāya paṃsusakkharamissāya. Aṅketi dvinnaṃ ūrūnaṃ majjhe. Miḍḍhanteti miḍḍhapariyante. Paribhaṇḍanteti bāhirapasse katāya tanukamiḍḍhiyā ante. Yo bhikkhu calakādiṃ vā patte ṭhapeyya, patte vā hatthadhovane hatthassa dhovanappaccayā tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho.

90-92. For one who places food in a container anywhere and eats it, there would be a dukkaṭa offense—this is the connection. If a bhikkhu holding a bowl were to move a window or a door, or heat a bowl with water, or expose it to the sun, or dry it, or if he were to overheat a bowl without water or leave it too long, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the meaning. If a bhikkhu were to place a bowl on the ground, on his lap, on a bed, on a stool, on a threshold, on a railing, on his foot, or on an umbrella, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the connection. 'On the ground' refers to any place mixed with dust or gravel serving no purpose. 'On the lap' means between the two thighs. 'On a threshold' means near the edge of a threshold. 'On a railing' means at the end of a thin low wall made on the outer side. If a bhikkhu were to place a cover, etc., on the bowl, or use the bowl for washing hands, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him due to the washing of hands—this is the connection.

93. Ucchiṭṭhaṃ mukhadhovanaṃ udakampi pattena nīharantassa bhikkhuno dukkaṭaṃ siyā. Yo bhikkhu akappiyaṃ pattaṃ paribhuñjeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Tattha akappiyaṃ pattanti dārumayapattādiṃ.

93. For a bhikkhu who removes leftovers or water for rinsing the mouth with a bowl, there would be a dukkaṭa offense. If a bhikkhu were to use an unsuitable bowl, that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the meaning. Here, 'unsuitable bowl' means a bowl made of wood and so on.

94. Yo bhikkhu khipite “jīvā”ti vade vadeyya, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti attho. Yo bhikkhu parimaṇḍalakādimhi pañcasattati sekhiye anādaro hutvā na sikkhati, tassa dukkaṭaṃ siyāti sambandho.

94. If a bhikkhu, when something is thrown, should say, 'It is alive!', that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the meaning. If a bhikkhu, being disrespectful, does not train in the seventy-five sekhiya rules beginning with 'Parimaṇḍala', that would be a dukkaṭa offense for him—this is the connection.

95. Yo bhikkhu bhaṇḍāgāre payuto mātuyā pituno ca bhaṇḍakaṃ gopeyya, assa bhikkhuno pācittiyaṃ siyāti sambandho. Tattha payutoti bhaṇḍāgāre byāpāravasena yuttappayutto. Gopayeti [V 0.0416] gopeyya. Yo bhikkhu [M 0.0495] davāya hīnena jātiādinā uttamampi vadeyya, dubbhāsitaṃ siyāti sambandho. Tattha hīnehi vā ukkaṭṭhehi vā jātiādīhi evaṃ ukkaṭṭhaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā “caṇḍālosī”tiādinā nayena ujuṃ vā “santi idhekacce caṇḍālavenanesādā”tiādinā nayena aññāpadesena vā upasampannaṃ vā anupasampannaṃ vā akkosādhippāyaṃ vinā kevalaṃ kīḷādhippāyena vadeyya, dubbhāsitaṃ siyāti.

95. If a bhikkhu, assigned to a storeroom, were to guard the belongings of his mother or father, for that bhikkhu there would be a pācittiya offense—this is the connection. Here, 'assigned' means engaged and employed in the business of the storeroom. 'To guard' means to protect. If a bhikkhu, for fun, were to address even a superior person with low terms such as birth, it would be wrong speech—this is the connection. Here, if one, with the mere intention of jest and without the intention to insult, should speak to a superior or an inferior person, whether ordained or unordained, using inferior or superior terms such as birth, either directly in the manner of 'You are an outcaste!' and so on, or indirectly in the manner of 'There are some outcastes, bamboo-workers, and hunters here,' and so on, it would be wrong speech.

Pakiṇṇakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of Miscellaneous Topics is concluded.

6. Vattādikaṇḍaniddesavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Section on Duties, etc.

96. Idāni vattaṃ dassetuṃ “upajjhācariyavatta”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha upajjhāyavattañca ācariyavattañca gamikavattañca āgantukavattañca senāsanādivattañca piyasīlena bhikkhunā kātabbanti sambandho. Gamikāgantukanti gamikaṃ āgantukanti chedo, gamikavattaṃ āgantukavattañcāti attho.

96. Now, to present the duties, 'the duties toward the preceptor and teacher' is stated. Herein, the duties toward the preceptor, the duties toward the teacher, the duties of one going on a journey, the duties of an incoming guest, and the duties regarding lodgings, etc., should be performed by a bhikkhu of amiable conduct—this is the connection. 'One going and an incoming guest' is separated into 'one going' and 'an incoming guest.' The meaning is the duties of one going on a journey and the duties of an incoming guest.

97. Dātukāmo hatthapāse ṭhito kiñci gahitabbaṃ ekena purisena gahitabbaṃ ukkhipanakkhamaṃ vatthuṃ tidhā tīsu pakāresu ekenākārena dadeyya, gahetukāmo bhikkhu dvidhā dvīsu ekena gaṇheyya, ayaṃ pañcaṅgo paṭiggahoti attho.

97. One who wishes to give, standing within arm's reach, should give an object that can be taken and lifted by one person, in one of three ways. The bhikkhu who wishes to receive should receive it in one of two ways. This is the five-factored receiving—this is the meaning.

98-100. Dūre ṭhitaṃ cīvaraṃ ṭhapitokāsaṃ sallakkhetvā “eta”nti vattabbaṃ. Hatthapāse ṭhitaṃ hatthena āmasitvā “ima”nti vattabbaṃ. “Etaṃ adhiṭṭhāmi, imaṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti imesaṃ padānaṃ majjhe saṅghāṭiādīsu paccekaṃ yojetvā ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭheyya. Kathaṃ? “Etaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmi, imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti adhiṭṭheyya. Evaṃ sesesu ca cīvaresu. Yathā cīvarādiṃ [M 0.0496] vidhānaṃ evaṃ pattepi adhiṭṭheyya paccuddhareyyāti attho.

98-100. For a robe placed at a distance, having noted its location, 'that' should be said. For one within arm's reach, having touched it with the hand, 'this' should be said. One should determine the three robes by applying one of these phrases, 'I determine that' or 'I determine this,' to each one, such as the outer robe, individually. How? One should determine it thus: 'I determine that outer robe,' or 'I determine this outer robe.' It is the same for the remaining robes. Just as is the procedure for the robes and so on, so too for the bowl, one should determine and relinquish it—this is the meaning.

101. Sañcarittaṃ ṭhapetvā sesā garukā ca pārājikā ca sacittakāti sambandho. Antimāti [V 0.0417] pārājikā. Acchinnasikkhāpadaṃ, pariṇatasikkhāpadañcāti imaṃ dvayaṃ ṭhapetvā sesaṃ nissaggiyaṃ acittakanti attho.

101. Except for acting as a go-between, the remaining grave offenses and offenses of defeat are intentional—this is the connection. The final ones are the offenses of defeat. Except for the training rule on undivided cloth and the training rule on diverted property, the rest of the offenses requiring forfeiture are unintentional—this is the meaning.

102-3. Gāmappavesananteteti gāmappavesanaṃ iti ete. Pācittīsu ete padasodhammādayo gāmappavesanantā sattarasa sikkhāpadā acittakā.

102-103. 'Ending with entering the village' means 'entering the village' and these. Among the pācittiya offenses, these seventeen training rules, beginning with teaching word by word and ending with entering the village, are unintentional.

104-5. Pakiṇṇakesu uddissakataṃ ṭhapetvā aññamaṃsakaṃ sesamaṃsaṃ acittakanti attho. Ettha pakiṇṇakesu aññamaṃsādikaṃ pattahattho kavāṭakantaṃ terasavidhaṃ idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ acittakaṃ, sesaṃ sabbaṃ sacittakanti attho.

104-105. Among the miscellaneous rules, except for meat specifically prepared, the remaining meat is unintentional—this is the meaning. Here, among the miscellaneous rules, these thirteen kinds of training rules, beginning with 'other meat' and ending with 'holding a bowl at the door', are unintentional; all the rest are intentional—this is the meaning.

106. Ācariyā vītikkamanacittena sacittakaṃ acittakanti vadanti, paññattijānanena cittena tathā sacittakaṃ acittakanti ācariyā vadantīti attho. Tathā-saddena “sacittakaṃ acittaka”nti idaṃ gahitaṃ.

106. Teachers say that an offense is intentional or unintentional depending on the transgressing mind; and teachers say that it is likewise intentional or unintentional depending on the mind that knows the rule—this is the meaning. By the word 'likewise,' the phrase 'intentional or unintentional' is included.

107-9. Pubbakaraṇādikanti ettha ādi-saddo pubbakiccaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Tattha –

107-109. 'Preliminary deeds, etc.'—here, the word 'etc.' includes preliminary tasks. In that connection:

“Sammajjanī padīpo ca, udakaṃ āsanena ca;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakaraṇanti vuccati.

Sweeping, a lamp, water, and a seat—these are called the preliminary deeds for the Uposatha.

“Chandapārisuddhiutukkhānaṃ, bhikkhugaṇanā ca ovādo;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakiccanti vuccatī”ti. –

Bringing of consent and purity, the declaration of the season, the counting of the bhikkhus, and the exhortation—these are called the preliminary tasks for the Uposatha.

Evaṃ pubbakaraṇādikaṃ navadhā dīpitaṃ sabbaṃ uposathappavāraṇaṃ piyasīlinā kātabbanti attho.

Thus, all the preliminary deeds and so on, which have been explained in nine ways, and the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā should be performed by one of amiable conduct—this is the meaning.

112. Yathākkamanti [M 0.0497] etthāyamadhippāyo – gaṇo pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kareyya, puggalo adhiṭṭhānauposathaṃ kareyya, saṅgho suttuddesauposathaṃ kareyyāti.

112. ‘In due order’: the meaning here is this—a group should perform the Uposatha of purity, an individual should perform the Uposatha of determination, and the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha of the recitation of the rule.

113. Cātuddaso pannaraso, sāmaggī dinato tidhāti cātuddaso uposatho[V 0.0418], pannaraso uposatho, sāmaggīuposathoti dinato tidhā honti. Dinato puggalato kattabbākārato te uposathā nava iti īritāti attho.

113. ‘On the fourteenth, on the fifteenth, and on the day of concord, thus threefold by day’: the fourteenth-day Uposatha, the fifteenth-day Uposatha, and the Uposatha of concord—thus they are threefold by day. By day, by person, and by the manner of performance, these Uposathas are said to be nine—this is the meaning.

114. Tevācī dvekavācīti tevācikā pavāraṇā, dvevācikā pavāraṇā, ekavācikā pavāraṇā iti nava pavāraṇā vuttā.

114. ‘With three utterances, with two, with one’: thus are spoken of the Pavāraṇā with three utterances, the Pavāraṇā with two utterances, and the Pavāraṇā with one utterance—nine Pavāraṇās in all.

115. Tassāti phaggunamāsassa. Tato sesanti āsāḷhiantimapakkhamhā yāva kattikapuṇṇamā vassakālanti attho. Ettha hi ekasmiṃ saṃvacchare catuvīsatiuposathā honti.

115. ‘Tassa’ means of the month of Phagguna. ‘Tato sesaṃ’ means from the last fortnight of Āsāḷha up to the full moon of Kattika is the rainy season—this is the meaning. Here, indeed, in one year there are twenty-four Uposathas.

116. Etesūti etesu tīsu catūsu ekekasmiṃ utumhi tatiyapakkhā sattamapakkhā. Cātuddasāti cha cātuddasāti attho. Sesāni uttānatthānevāti.

116. ‘Etesu’ means: in each of these three or four seasons, the third and seventh fortnights. ‘Cātuddasā’ means six fourteenths; this is the meaning. The remaining parts are of clear meaning.

Vattādikaṇḍaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Section on Duties and so forth is concluded.

Nigamanakathā

Concluding Discourse

Ettāvatā [M 0.0498] samāraddhā, mūlasikkhatthavaṇṇanā;

Niṭṭhitā yā samāsena, aḍḍhamāsassa accaye.

The explanation of the meaning of the Root Training, thus undertaken, has been completed in brief with the passing of half a month.

Adhunūpasampannānaṃ, hitatthāya samāsato;

Imaṃ atthaṃ vaṇṇayatā, yaṃ puññaṃdhigataṃ mayā.

Whatever merit has been acquired by me in explaining this meaning in brief for the benefit of the newly ordained,

Tena puññenayaṃ loko, sukhāya paṭipattiyā;

Pāpuṇātu visuddhāya, nibbānaṃ ajaraṃ padaṃ.

by that merit, may this world, through pure practice, attain the ageless state of Nibbāna for the sake of happiness.

Nānātarugaṇākiṇṇe[V 0.0419], nānākusalakāmino;

Ramme yuddhānapatino, vihāre vasatā satā.

Dwelling mindfully in the delightful monastery, free from strife, filled with various kinds of trees and with those who desire diverse wholesome states,

Sāsane siddhipattassa, siddhinā ñāṇasiddhinā;

Paṇḍitena katā esā, mūlasikkhatthavaṇṇanā.

this explanation of the meaning of the Root Training was composed by the wise Siddhi, who has attained success in the Dispensation through the success of knowledge.

Mūlasikkhā-ṭīkā samattā.

The Sub-commentary on the Root Training is concluded.
